brief_summary:
Minimally invasive techniques for colorectal surgery include standard laparoscopy and robot-assisted laparoscopy. Studies evaluating recovery after anaesthesia and surgery have focused primarily on physiological endpoints, recovery times, and the incidence of adverse events, such as major morbidity and mortality. Although these parameters are essential and should be measured, they mostly ignore the patient's perspective. Patient-related outcomes can be assessed with tools designed for that purpose, such as the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) questionnaire.

This single-centre prospective observational cohort study will compare robotic vs laparoscopic colorectal resections with the primary outcome of QoR-15 at 24 hours after surgery, capturing anaesthesia-specific variables to adjust for confounding.
primary_outcomes: Primary outcome: Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) total score at 24 hours after surgery (±4 h window).
title: Quality of Recovery After Colorectal Surgery (Robots vs Laparoscopic)

brief_summary:
Pancreatic cancer (specifically pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, PDAC) is a very aggressive disease that is often diagnosed too late for surgery, and the medicines currently available, mainly two chemotherapy combinations called modified FOLFIRINOX (mFFX) and gemcitabine + nab-paclitaxel (GnP), can extend life but rarely cure patients.

This study examines mefloquine, a well-studied antimalarial drug, as a new way to attack pancreatic cancer. Laboratory work has shown that mefloquine can block an enzyme (TYMS) that cancer cells need to make DNA, and unlike many existing drugs it does not cause the cancer cells to produce more of that enzyme and become resistant. In several mouse models, as well as tumors grown from human patients, oral mefloquine at doses that were well tolerated (up to 300 mg/kg) slowed tumor growth and helped the animals live longer.

This trial aims to find a safe dose of mefloquine for PDAC patients. A classic "3 + 3" design will be used in three separate arms: one taking mFFX, one taking GnP, and one taking mefloquine as monotherapy after exhausting standard of care treatment options. The main goals are to determine the recommended Phase 2 dose and to collect early signals that the drug might help shrink tumors when combined with existing chemotherapy. If the trial shows that mefloquine can be given safely and hints at improved tumor control, it would pave the way for larger studies that could eventually add an established and already-approved drug to the existing treatment options for advanced pancreatic cancer.
primary_outcomes: Recommended phase 2 dose
title: Repurposing Mefloquine for Pancreatic Cancer Treatment

brief_summary: This is a prospective, observational cohort study. The primary objective is to characterize the clinical features and mechanisms of behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia (BPSD) in patients with probable Alzheimer's disease (AD) who are plasma p-Tau217 negative, and to compare them with p-Tau217-positive patients. After grouping participants by an authoritative p-Tau217 cutoff value, the negative and positive groups will be systematically compared across all 12 domains of the Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI). Participants will be followed up at 6, 12, and 18 months to compare the incidence of cognitive decline, new-onset severe BPSD (hallucinations, agitation/aggression, depression, etc.), cerebrovascular events, and hospitalization between the two groups. As an exploratory objective, baseline BPSD domains combined with imaging (white matter hyperintensity burden) and blood biomarkers (NfL, IL-6, GFAP, etc.) will be used to construct a simple prognostic risk-stratification model within the negative group and to validate its predictive performance. The study aims to improve the recognition of non-AD-driven dementia with overlapping clinical presentations, thereby informing clinical management and care planning in the era of biology-based AD diagnosis.
primary_outcomes: Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI)
Mini-Mental State Examination（MMSE）
Montreal Cognitive Assessment（MoCA）
title: Study on Clinical Characteristics of Patients With Probable Alzheimer's Dementia Stratified by Blood Biomarkers

brief_summary:
This is a multicenter, prospective, pragmatic, randomized controlled trial (IMPROVE-STEMI) aiming to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intracoronary low-dose recombinant streptokinase combined with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI) in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

A total of 3,300 patients will be enrolled, consisting of a core randomized study (300 patients, 1:1 ratio to pPCI + recombinant streptokinase vs. pPCI alone) and an extended observational study (3,000 patients receiving pPCI + recombinant streptokinase). The primary outcome measure is the coronary angiography-derived index of microcirculatory resistance (caIMR) immediately after the procedure. Secondary outcomes include the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) at 1 year, TIMI flow grade, corrected TIMI frame count (CTFC), and myocardial salvage index.

The study duration is 24 months after the first patient enrollment, with follow-up visits scheduled at Day 5, Week 4, Week 12, Week 24, and Week 52.
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University
primary_outcomes: Coronary Angiography-derived Index of Microcirculatory Resistance (caIMR)
title: IMPROVE-STEMI: pPCI Plus Low-dose r-SK in STEMI

brief_summary:
Large-to-Massive rotator cuff tears of the shoulder with poor tendon and muscle quality often cannot be fully repaired back to its footprint, and they have a high risk of re-tear. This study evaluates a combined technique for these tears.

During surgery, the torn rotator cuff is repaired as far as possible, the long head of the biceps tendon is transposed (rerouted) and fixed to the top of the humeral head, and the repair is augmented with an acellular dermal matrix graft (MegaDerm Plus, L\&C Bio, Republic of Korea). All participants receive the same operation and the same structured rehabilitation program; there is no comparison group.

Forty adults aged 40 to 75 years treated at Tam Anh General Hospital, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, will be followed for at least 12 months after surgery. The main outcome is the rate of tendon retear on MRI at 12 months. Pain, shoulder function scores (Constant, ASES, UCLA), range of motion, muscle strength, X-ray findings and complications, including graft-related complications, will also be recorded.
primary_outcomes: Rotator Cuff Retear Rate on MRI
title: Biceps Tendon- Superior Capsule Reconstruction and Acellular Dermal Matrix Augmentation for Large to Massive Incompletely Repairable Rotator Cuff Tears

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate myocardial reperfusion in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).

Although primary PCI successfully restores blood flow in the blocked coronary artery, some patients continue to have impaired blood flow within the small vessels of the heart muscle, a condition known as microvascular obstruction (MVO). This complication may be associated with greater myocardial injury and poorer clinical outcomes.

The study will investigate whether artificial intelligence (AI)-derived electrocardiographic (ECG) features, coronary angiographic parameters, and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) findings can provide complementary information about myocardial reperfusion.

Patients undergoing primary PCI will be assessed using ECG and angiographic findings, while CMR will be used to evaluate myocardial injury and microvascular obstruction.

The main objective is to determine whether combining AI-derived ECG features and angiographic parameters can improve the prediction of CMR-detected microvascular obstruction after primary PCI.

The findings may help identify patients at increased risk of impaired myocardial reperfusion and support future risk assessment strategies following STEMI.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Cardiac MRI-Detected Microvascular Obstruction After Primary PCI
title: Multimodality Assessment of Myocardial Reperfusion After Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention

brief_summary: This study compared two ways of preparing discharge documents for children and families leaving a pediatric emergency department. In the usual workflow, information from the electronic health record was assembled into a fixed document template. In the alternative workflow, ERIOS Assistant, an artificial intelligence system hosted within the hospital, drafted documents for health professionals and for families or children. A clinician reviewed and validated the documents before they were handed to the family in both workflows. According to the completed study report, assignment concerned document production after the decision to discharge and did not determine diagnosis, treatment or disposition. Families were contacted by telephone after discharge to assess how their account of the care and instructions agreed with the medical record, as well as their perceived understanding, satisfaction and use of the documents. The protocol also planned assessment of document quality, readability, clinician experience, usability and human supervision. This study is being registered retrospectively after the randomized component was completed.
primary_outcomes: Record-Concordant Family Understanding After Discharge
title: AI-Assisted Discharge Documents for Children and Families in a Pediatric Emergency Department

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn how accurately an artificial intelligence (AI) software called Prostate Intelligence (Pi) detects clinically significant prostate cancer on prostate MRI in adults with a prostate gland who are referred for MRI because prostate cancer is suspected.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- How sensitive and specific is Pi, used on its own, in detecting clinically significant prostate cancer (Gleason grade 3+4 or higher) at the patient level?

Researchers will also compare Pi, the radiologist alone, and the radiologist assisted by Pi, to see whether AI assistance changes cancer detection.

Participants will:

* Undergo prostate MRI as part of their usual clinical care. Each MRI is first read by a radiologist without the AI result; the Pi report is then shown to the radiologist, who produces a final combined report.
* Undergo targeted prostate biopsy (up to two lesions) if the MRI is suspicious, as in routine practice. Areas flagged only by Pi may also be biopsied.
* If not biopsied, be followed for 12 months after MRI with PSA tests at 6 and 12 months and clinical assessment, to confirm the absence of clinically significant cancer.

About 226 participants will be enrolled at two Italian centres (Fondazione Policlinico Universitario A. Gemelli IRCCS, Rome, and IRCCS Ospedale San Raffaele, Milan).
lead_sponsor: Fondazione Policlinico Universitario Agostino Gemelli IRCCS
primary_outcomes: Patient-level sensitivity of Pi stand-alone for clinically significant prostate cancer (Gleason score >=3+4)
Patient-level specificity of Pi stand-alone for clinically significant prostate cancer (Gleason score >=3+4)
title: Artificial Intelligence Software (Prostate Intelligence) for Detecting Clinically Significant Prostate Cancer on MRI

brief_summary:
Carpal tunnel syndrome can cause numbness, tingling, pain, and reduced hand function. The Phalen test is commonly used during clinical examination, but it is usually recorded only as positive or negative. The time needed for the symptoms caused by the test to return to their pre-test level may provide additional information about the clinical severity of carpal tunnel syndrome.

This study will investigate the clinical meaning of symptom recovery time after the Phalen test in adults with electrodiagnostically confirmed carpal tunnel syndrome. During the test, participants will keep their wrists fully flexed for up to 60 seconds. If typical symptoms appear or clearly increase, the test will be stopped and the wrists will be returned to a neutral position. The time required for symptoms to return to their pre-test level will be recorded.

Participants will also complete the Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire and will be evaluated for nighttime symptoms and nerve conduction findings. The study will examine whether recovery time is related to hand function, symptom severity, nighttime complaints, symptom onset time during the Phalen test, and electrodiagnostic severity. A subgroup of participants with a positive Phalen test will repeat the test after 3-7 days to evaluate its test-retest reliability. No treatment will be assigned as part of this observational study.
primary_outcomes: Symptom Recovery Time After the Phalen Test
title: Symptom Recovery Time After the Phalen Test in Carpal Tunnel Syndrome

brief_summary: In recent years, the use of autologously obtained blood products that stimulate cell proliferation, such as platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and platelet-rich fibrin (PRF), has become increasingly widespread. Numerous studies have been published on PRF, which comes in many different forms. I-PRF, an injectable form, requires a lower cycle time and has a higher growth factor. Conventional root canal treatment remains effective in the treatment of periapical lesions. However, the treatment course can vary, and lesion size may remain constant even after the termination of root canal treatment, even if symptoms resolve. Therefore, our study aimed to achieve greater bone trabeculation and a greater reduction in lesion size compared to conventional treatment in the treatment of relatively large lesions (0.3-1 cm) by injecting I-PRF into the apical lesion area at several points and in three sessions. To this end, to more clearly demonstrate healing and to examine trabeculations in detail, cone-beam computed tomography images will be obtained on the day the apical lesions are diagnosed (day 1) and at the second follow-up appointment (month 6). If our study results are significant, it will be possible to salvage teeth with apical lesions, often considered for extraction, with a cost-effective treatment option.
interventions: root canal treatment and intracanal medicament
primary_outcomes: reduction in lesion volume
title: The Effect of Injectable Platelet Rich Fibrin on Apical Lesion Healing

brief_summary:
Children who survive critical illness may develop new or worsening problems with physical health, cognitive status, emotional well-being, and social functioning. These problems, collectively known as post-intensive care syndrome in pediatrics (PICS-p), may also affect family well-being. Evidence on how frequently these problems occur, how they change over time, and which factors influence recovery remains limited in China.

This single-center, prospective observational cohort study at Children's Hospital of Fudan University aims to describe the occurrence and recovery trajectories of PICS-p and identify factors associated with persistent difficulties or recovery. The study focuses on children admitted to the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with sepsis, severe pneumonia or acute respiratory distress syndrome, those receiving cranial neurosurgical care, and those requiring prolonged mechanical ventilation.

Clinical information and standardized assessments will be collected to evaluate physical function, overall quality of life, cognitive function, psychological well-being, social functioning, and family outcomes. Follow-up will include assessments at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after PICU discharge, with longer-term follow-up planned at 2 years, 3 years, and beyond. The study will examine how outcomes change over time and identify potentially modifiable risk factors.

The findings will help identify early which children and families need additional support and guide the development of rehabilitation and coordinated follow-up care across hospital, home, and community settings.
primary_outcomes: Health-Related Quality of Life Assessed by the PedsQL 4.0 Generic Core Scales Total Score
Proportion of Children With Physical Functional Impairment
Proportion of Children With Cognitive Impairment
Proportion of Children With Psychological Impairment
Proportion of Children With Social Functional Impairment
Proportion of Families With Impaired Family Functioning
title: PICS-p Longitudinal Cohort Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if Iparomlimab/Tuvonralimab combined with nab-paclitaxel and cisplatin as neoadjuvant treatment can treat locally advanced cervical cancer in adult female patients. It will also learn about the safety of this combination regimen. The main questions it aims to answer are:

What is the pathological complete response (pCR) rate after neoadjuvant combination therapy? What are the objective response rate, progression-free survival, overall survival, biomarker changes and tumor immune microenvironment changes in participants receiving this regimen?

There is no comparison group in this single-arm study.

Participants will:

* Receive neoadjuvant treatment with Iparomlimab/Tuvonralimab, albumin-bound paclitaxel and cisplatin
* Undergo radical surgery after completion of neoadjuvant therapy
* Receive scheduled imaging, blood and tissue biomarker tests
* Be followed up regularly for survival and safety assessment.
primary_outcomes: Pathological complete response (pCR) rate
title: Iparomlimab/Tuvonralimab Combined With Nab-paclitaxel and Cisplatin as Neoadjuvant Therapy for Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer

brief_summary:
In this randomized, controlled, double-blind clinical trial, we will follow adult participants who receive partial or full dental crowns made of lithium disilicate ceramic (LDC). Before the crowns are permanently attached to teeth, those in the control group will be etched with hydrofluoric acid (HF) according to the standard laboratory protocol, while those in the intervention group will undergo an innovative surface treatment with atmospheric-pressure nonthermal plasma (APP).

The goal of this study is to determine whether the innovative APP pretreatment of LDC crowns can result in outcomes comparable to or better than those achieved with the standard HF treatment, including:

* oral health-related quality of life as reported by the participants; and
* the clinical success and survival of LDC crowns.

Participants will be asked to attend scheduled follow-up visits 1 week and 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after the crowns are cemented. At each visit:

* a researcher will examine the crowns and surrounding teeth and tissues for any biological or technical complications; and
* participants will complete a questionnaire to assess their oral health-related quality of life.
interventions: Hydrofluoric Acid-Etched Lithium Disilicate Ceramic Dental Crowns
Atmospheric-Pressure Plasma-Treated Lithium Disilicate Ceramic Dental Crowns
lead_sponsor: University of Ljubljana, Faculty of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Oral Health-Related Quality of Life (OHIP Score)
Clinical Success of Partial- and Full-Coverage Dental Crowns Made of Lithium Disilicate Ceramic
title: Evaluation of Ceramic Dental Crown Clinical Performance After Conventional Hydrofluoric Acid Etching or Gaseous Plasma Pretreatment

brief_summary:
Overweight and obesity are long-term health conditions that can increase the possibility of serious health problems. These problems include heart disease, type 2 diabetes (a condition that causes high blood sugar), and other medical conditions. The purpose of this study is to learn whether berobenatide (PF-08653944) is safe and effective for adults in China who are overweight or obese. Researchers will compare berobenatide with a placebo. A placebo looks like study treatment but does not contain active medicine.

About 432 adults will take part in this study. This study is seeking adults who

* are obese
* are overweight with certain weight-related health conditions. Some participants may also have type 2 diabetes. Specific eligibility requirements will be reviewed by the study doctor before enrollment.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either berobenatide or placebo. Study treatment will be administered as a shot under the skin. All participants will also receive lifestyle counseling throughout the study.

Researchers will monitor participants throughout the study. They will assess participants' body weight, overall health, and any reactions that may occur. During the study, participants will attend study visits and complete study-related assessments.

Participants may take part in the study for up to approximately 59 weeks. This period includes screening, treatment, and follow-up visits. The information learned from this study may help researchers better understand whether berobenatide could be a treatment option for adults living with overweight or obesity.
primary_outcomes: Percent change from baseline in body weight
title: A Study to Learn About the Study Medicine Called PF-08653944 Taken Once-Monthly Compared to Placebo in Chinese Adults With Overweight or Obesity

brief_summary: This prospective, observational, comparative diagnostic study will evaluate the performance of Radiofrequency Echographic Multi Spectrometry (REMS) for the diagnosis of osteoporosis and prediction of fragility fracture risk in a U.S. population, using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) as the reference standard. Approximately 250 male and female participants aged 30-90 years who are undergoing evaluation for bone health will be enrolled at Rheumatology Associates of Delmarva. Participants will have clinically obtained DXA results and undergo REMS assessment of the lumbar spine and proximal femur. Diagnostic performance, including sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and concordance between REMS and DXA, will be evaluated. Participants will also be followed by telephone at 6 and 12 months to identify incident non-traumatic fragility fractures and assess the ability of REMS and DXA to predict fracture risk.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic concordance between REMS and DXA
Diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of REMS for osteoporosis compared with DXA

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either Ketadex or Ketofol. The study will also compare recovery time, hemodynamic effects, pain, emergence reactions, nausea and vomiting, and other adverse events between the two groups. brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a corneal preservation solution can safely and effectively preserve donor corneas for corneal transplantation in patients who need penetrating keratoplasty (PKP) or endothelial keratoplasty (EK). It will also learn about the safety of this corneal preservation solution. The main questions it aims to answer are:

What is the donor viability rate on the day of transplantation, defined as the proportion of donor corneas with endothelial cell density (ECD) ≥2,000 cells/mm²? What is the corneal graft transparency rate 14 days after transplantation? What medical problems do participants have after transplantation? This is a single-center, prospective, single-arm study. Researchers will enroll 60 patients at Shandong Provincial Eye Hospital (Affiliated Eye Hospital of Shandong First Medical University). All participants will receive a donor cornea preserved in the corneal preservation solution for 2-7 days. Donor corneal ECD and hexagonality will be measured at the time of donor retrieval and on the day of transplantation. Donors with ECD ≥2,000 cells/mm² can be used for transplantation. Participants will be followed for 14 days after transplantation. There is no comparison group.

Participants will:

Undergo PKP or EK using a donor cornea preserved in the corneal preservation solution for 2-7 days.

Have donor corneal ECD and hexagonality measured before transplantation. Be followed for 14 days after transplantation for graft transparency, ECD, graft thickness, epithelial healing, visual acuity recovery, secondary surgery, and adverse events.

The results will provide evidence for the formal clinical use of this corneal preservation solution in China.
primary_outcomes: Donor Corneal Viability Rate
Corneal Graft Transparency Rate
title: Safety and Efficacy of Corneal Preservation Solution: A Prospective Single-Arm Study

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate how parents or legal guardians perceive responsibility for surgical risk after the informed consent discussion for their child's operation, focusing on whether the process feels like "risk sharing" with the clinical team or "risk dumping" onto the parent. In pediatric surgery, parents often serve as surrogate decision-makers, and little is known about how consent conversations shape feelings of support, blame, trust, and decisional burden.

Using a mixed-methods, cross-sectional design, the study will recruit parents/legal guardians of children under 18 years of age undergoing pediatric surgical procedures at Comer Children's Hospital after the clinical consent discussion and before surgery. Participants will complete a post-consent survey assessing perceptions of risk sharing versus risk dumping, understanding of risks and benefits, satisfaction with the consent process, trust in the surgeon/institution, decisional conflict, anxiety, and relevant demographic and clinical factors. A subset of participants will also complete semi-structured interviews to further explore experiences of responsibility, blame, institutional support, and suggestions for improving the consent process.

The goal is to characterize parental perceptions of responsibility in pediatric surgical consent and identify communication, demographic, and clinical factors associated with greater perceived risk dumping. Findings may help inform interventions to improve informed consent and shared decision-making practices in pediatric surgery.
conditions: Parental Decision Making for Seriously Ill Children
primary_outcomes: Parental perception of risk sharing versus risk dumping after pediatric surgical informed consent
title: Risk Sharing vs Risk Dumping: Parental Attitudes About Risks

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to identify predictors of successful removal of benign intrauterine pathology using a mini-resectoscope during office operative hysteroscopy without anesthesia in adult women with suspected or diagnosed endometrial polyps or retained products of conception up to 2.5 cm in size.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Which demographic, gynecologic, clinical, and hysteroscopic factors are associated with successful completion of office operative hysteroscopy using a mini-resectoscope without anesthesia?
* Which factors are associated with severe pain during the procedure, defined as a Visual Analog Scale (VAS) score greater than 7?
* Is prolonged procedure duration (\>3 minutes) associated with higher intraoperative pain scores?
* Are there differences in success rates between procedures performed for endometrial polyps versus retained products of conception?

Participants will:

* Undergo office operative hysteroscopy without anesthesia using the Miniresectoscope device for removal of endometrial polyps or retained products of conception.
* Provide demographic, obstetric, gynecologic, and medical history information before the procedure.
* Have intraoperative hysteroscopic and surgical characteristics recorded, including cervical stenosis, uterine orientation, lesion size and location, lesion morphology, and procedure duration.
* Complete pain assessments using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) during the procedure and 5 minutes after the procedure.
* Be evaluated for procedural success, defined as complete removal of the intrauterine pathology.

brief_summary:
Many youth experience ongoing stomach pain that does not have a clear medical cause. These conditions, called functional abdominal pain disorders, are common and can last for years. They often interfere with school attendance, daily activities, and social life, and are frequently linked with anxiety. Families may go through many medical tests and appointments without finding relief. The investigators' research shows that teaching these children coping skills, such as relaxation, problem solving, and managing anxious thoughts, can reduce pain and improve functioning.

The Aim to Decrease Anxiety and Pain Treatment (ADAPT) is a brief program developed by the investigators that uses cognitive behavioral strategies and mindfulness to help children manage pain and anxiety. However, access to providers trained to deliver these types of psychological treatments can be limited, creating a need for more accessible treatment options. The purpose of this project is to culturally adapt ADAPT for youth in Spain and deliver it through a digital platform, allowing children and families to access the program without requiring a trained provider to deliver each session. The project will evaluate how well the culturally adapted digital program works and whether it can be successfully delivered to youth in Spain. The goal is to increase access to evidence-based care, reduce pain and anxiety symptoms, and improve daily functioning for youth with functional abdominal pain disorders.
interventions: Aim to Decrease Anxiety and Pain Treatment (ADAPT)
primary_outcomes: Retention Rates
Feasibility of intervention
title: ADAPTing CBT for Pediatric Functional Abdominal Pain in Spain

brief_summary: Flutter therapy is an oscillating positive expiratory pressure (OPEP) technique that combines positive expiratory pressure with airway oscillations to facilitate mobilization and clearance of respiratory secretions. Conventional chest physiotherapy includes deep breathing exercises, incentive spirometry, airway-clearance techniques, splinted coughing and early mobilization to promote lung expansion and secretion clearance. A total of 94 patients aged 40-70 years with mild-to-moderate COPD undergoing elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) will be enrolled in this randomized controlled trial and will be randomly allocated into two groups, with 47 participants in each group. The intervention group will receive conventional chest physiotherapy combined with Flutter therapy, while the control group will receive conventional chest physiotherapy alone. Both groups will receive supervised treatment for 5 consecutive postoperative days, with 3 sessions per day, resulting in 15 treatment sessions. Baseline assessment will be performed on postoperative day 1 before commencement of the intervention, and post-intervention assessment will be conducted on postoperative day 5. The study will compare the effects of Flutter-assisted conventional chest physiotherapy versus conventional chest physiotherapy alone on postoperative peak expiratory flow rate, chest expansion and airway clearance.

primary_outcomes: Peak Expiratory Flow Rate
Chest Expansion
title: Additional Effects of Flutter With Conventional Chest Physiotherapy on Peak Expiratory Flow Rate and Chest Expansion in Post CABG Patients With COPD

brief_summary:
The Real-World Drug-Coated Balloon Registry (RW-DCB) is an investigator-initiated, multicenter, observational cohort study evaluating the use of drug-coated balloons (DCBs) during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) in routine clinical practice. The registry will include consecutive adults in whom a coronary DCB strategy is planned or attempted, regardless of the clinical presentation, lesion type, DCB platform, success of lesion preparation, successful delivery of the DCB, or final treatment strategy.

The study does not assign any treatment or require additional procedures, tests, or visits. All clinical decisions, including lesion preparation, device selection, use of intracoronary imaging or physiology, antithrombotic therapy, and follow-up, remain at the discretion of the treating team.

The retrospective cohort will include eligible procedures performed from January 2022 until prospective data collection begins at each participating center. Prospective enrollment will continue for at least 24 months after activation of the first center. Each participant will be followed for up to 24 months after the index procedure.

The primary outcome is target lesion failure at 12 months, defined as cardiovascular death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or clinically indicated target lesion revascularization. The registry will also evaluate procedural outcomes, DCB delivery failure, changes in treatment strategy, bailout stenting, other clinical events, antithrombotic treatment, and outcomes associated with lesion preparation and specific DCB platforms. The operational target is at least 2,000 participants, with no upper enrollment limit.
primary_outcomes: Target Lesion Failure
title: Real-World Outcomes of Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Coronary Artery Disease

A total of 120 toddlers with ASD will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either an intervention group or a usual care group.

Participants in the intervention group will receive standardized maternal interactive massage in addition to usual care and ASD parenting guidance, whereas participants in the usual care group will receive usual care and ASD parenting guidance only. The interactive massage will be performed by the child's mother for 15 minutes per session, three sessions per day, six days per week, for three months.

The primary outcome is parent-child interaction quality. Secondary outcomes include salivary oxytocin levels and brain responses to social versus non-social stimuli measured using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, immediately after the 3-month intervention, and at a 1-month post-intervention follow-up.

brief_summary:
The aim of this study is to evaluate the effect of artificial intelligence-supported training and the Benson relaxation exercise on the care burden and stress levels of caregivers of people with Parkinson's disease. In the study, caregivers of people with Parkinson's disease will receive training on caring for people with Parkinson's disease and on the Benson relaxation exercise. The training sessions will be conducted using an artificial intelligence-based module. Participants will be randomly assigned to three groups: a training group, an exercise group, and a control group. A caregiver information form, the Modified Hoehn and Yahr Scale, the Zarit Caregiver Burden Scale, and the Caregiver Stress Scale will be used to collect pretest data from all participants during the initial interview. The training sessions for the experimental group will last 4 weeks. No training will be provided to the control group. Four weeks later, the Zarit Caregiver Burden Scale and the Caregiver Stress Scale will be used to collect final test data from the experimental and control groups.

The hypotheses related to this study are as follows:

* Artificial intelligence-supported training provided to caregivers of people with Parkinson's disease affects the burden of care.
* The Benson relaxation exercise provided to caregivers of people with Parkinson's disease affects the burden of care.
* Artificial intelligence-supported training provided to caregivers of people with Parkinson's disease affects stress levels.
* The Benson relaxation exercise administered to caregivers of people with Parkinson's disease affects stress levels.
primary_outcomes: Zarit Caregiver Burden Scale
Caregiver Stress Scale
title: Effect of Artificial Intelligent-based Training and Benson Relaxation Exercises on Caregiver Burden and Stress Levels in Caregivers of Patients With Parkinson's Disease

brief_summary: Neurological outcome is the primary outcome for post-cardiac arrest patients. Hypoxic-ischemic brain injury is a key element in post-cardiac arrest syndrome, and remains the leading cause of mortality and morbidity in post-cardiac arrest patients. In patients with hypoxic-ischemic brain injury, impaired cerebral autoregulation makes cerebral blood flow highly vulnerable to blood pressure fluctuations, which might trigger secondary brain injuries. Although the pressure reactivity index (PRx) calculated via invasive intracranial pressure (ICP) monitoring is considered the gold standard for assessing cerebral autoregulation, its clinical application in post-cardiac arrest patients is limited due to invasive risks. Alternatively, cerebral near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) combined with hemodynamic monitoring offers a non-invasive approach to measure the cerebral oxygenation index (COx). However, its consistency with invasive methods and its accuracy in post-cardiac arrest care warrant further validation. The aim of this study is to assess cerebral autoregulation via COx calculated with NIRS and hemodynamic parameters in post-cardiac arrest patients, and to analyze the impact of this index on neurological outcomes. The further goal is to estimate optimal mean arterial pressure (MAPopt) and subsequently establish personalized post-resuscitation blood pressure targets.
primary_outcomes: Neurological Outcome
title: Integrated Near-Infrared Spectroscopy and Hemodynamic Monitoring for Cerebral Autoregulation in Post-Cardiac Arrest Care Neuroprognostication

brief_summary:
Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a leading cause of preventable liver-related morbidity and mortality, with hospitalizations for ALD increasing significantly in recent years. Many patients with ALD and active alcohol use disorder (AUD) are discharged from the hospital without receiving evidence-based behavioral interventions, despite hospitalization representing a teachable moment when patients may be more motivated to change. Psychosocial support in this setting is often limited by short inpatient stays, provider shortages, and workflow barriers. Novel digital health approaches are needed to increase access to structured, personalized behavioral support during hospitalization.

This project aims to assess the feasibility, usability, and clinical relevance of SOBER-VR, a virtual reality (VR) and artificial intelligence (AI)-powered digital therapeutic that delivers motivational interviewing (MI) to hospitalized patients with ALD and active alcohol use. SOBER-VR uses immersive VR to enhance emotional salience and a large language model (LLM)-driven conversational agent to simulate reflective, MI-consistent interactions. The intervention is brief (10-15 minutes), self-guided, and delivered using sanitized, standalone VR headsets with real-time support from trained staff.

Using the NIH ORBIT Model for behavioral intervention development, this Phase Ib single-arm feasibility study will recruit 30 hospitalized patients with ALD and active alcohol use. Participants will use SOBER-VR during their inpatient stay and complete structured assessments post-discharge. The study will evaluate feasibility (recruitment, engagement, and retention), acceptability, usability, and safety of SOBER-VR. Preliminary signals of clinical impact, such as readiness to change, attitude to AUD treatment, among others, will also be explored.
primary_outcomes: SOBER-VR Intervention Feasibility, calculated by eligibility yield, consent rate, intervention uptake, and follow-up completion percentages
System Usability Scale (SUS) of SOBER-VR
SOBER-VR Acceptability through qualitative satisfaction ratings
Incidence of Adverse Events
title: An AI-powered Virtual Reality Brief Intervention for Hospitalized Patients With Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease (SOBER-VR)

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled experimental study examined the effects of a brief self-compassion intervention program (BSCIP) on mental health outcomes among adolescents reporting four or more adverse childhood experiences (ACEs).

The study used a randomized controlled pre-test-post-test-follow-up design with a control group. Adolescents who met the eligibility criteria were randomly assigned to an intervention group or a control group. The intervention group received a structured four-session BSCIP, while the control group did not receive any structured intervention during the study period.

The BSCIP was based on self-compassion theory and included psychoeducational content and experiential exercises focusing on self-kindness, mindfulness, and common humanity. The program was delivered in a school setting.

Outcome assessments were conducted at pre-test, post-test, and 3-month follow-up. Primary outcomes included stress, anxiety, and depression symptoms, assessed using the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale (DASS-21). Secondary outcomes included self-compassion, life satisfaction, and psychological well-being, assessed using validated self-report measures. Data were analyzed using a two-way mixed analysis of variance.
conditions: Adverse Childhood Experiences and Adolescent Mental Health
primary_outcomes: Stress symptoms
Anxiety symptoms
Depressive symptoms
title: Self-Compassion Based Psychoeducation Program for Adolescents With Adverse Childhood Experiences

brief_summary:

Forty-five healthy premenopausal women aged 18-45 with regular menstrual cycles and self-reported recurrent premenstrual symptoms will be enrolled.

The study spans approximately 12 weeks across three consecutive menstrual cycles. Cycle 1 serves as a no-product baseline cycle during which participants complete validated questionnaires on Day 5. During Cycles 2 and 3, participants take two Day capsules each morning and two Night capsules each evening, beginning 7 days before their anticipated period and continuing through Day 2 of their cycle. Questionnaires are completed on Day 5 of each product cycle. All study activities are conducted remotely via the Citruslabs digital study platform; there are no in-person visits, blood draws, or laboratory procedures.

brief_summary:
This prospective observational study aims to evaluate adherence to preoperative fasting guidelines and investigate the relationship between actual fasting durations, anxiety levels, and blood glucose levels in children aged 1-10 years undergoing elective circumcision under general anesthesia.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Are the actual preoperative fasting durations in children longer than the recommended fasting durations?

Are prolonged fasting durations associated with increased preoperative anxiety levels in children?

Is there a relationship between fasting durations and parental anxiety levels?

Are prolonged fasting durations associated with preoperative blood glucose levels in children?

Do parental educational levels influence adherence to preoperative fasting recommendations?

The study will include children aged 1-10 years who are scheduled to undergo elective circumcision under general anesthesia at Yahyali State Hospital, Kayseri, Türkiye.

Parents will be asked to report the last time their children consumed solid foods and clear liquids, and actual fasting durations will be calculated. Before surgery, children's anxiety levels will be assessed using the Modified Yale Preoperative Anxiety Scale (m-YPAS), while parental anxiety levels will be evaluated using the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory-State (STAI-State). Preoperative blood glucose levels will also be measured.

No experimental treatments or interventions will be performed, and participation in the study will not result in any changes to routine anesthesia, surgical procedures, or perioperative care.
primary_outcomes: Preoperative Anxiety Level in Children
title: PREOPERATIVE FASTING AND PERIOPERATIVE OUTCOMES IN CHILDREN UNDERGOING ELECTIVE CIRCUMCISION

brief_summary: This single-site, biomarker-enriched, randomized Phase II study will evaluate osimertinib with or without cyclosporine A (CsA) in metastatic epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR )-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) \[exon 19 deletion or L858R\]. All consented, baseline circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-positive patients receive a 3-week osimertinib run-in; those with persistent ctDNA ("shedders") are randomized 1:1 to continue osimertinib or osimertinib+CsA. Plasma is collected approximately every 3 weeks in both arms for molecular response monitoring. The investigators plan to enroll 60 patients with approximately 40 "shedders" randomized with 20 enrolled in each arm. All patients will be treated with osimertinib daily throughout the study; the combination of osimertinib+CsA will receive CsA. Imaging will be performed as per standard of care.
conditions: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer With Mutation in Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor
