title: SPGL008 in Combination With SSGJ-706 ± Chemotherapy for Advanced Non-small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary:
This study will look at how different amounts of the study medicine, called PF-08656795, are tolerated and act in adults with overweight or obesity.

Doctors will check if each person meets the study conditions, including age, body weight, and general health. People with certain medical conditions will not be able to take part in the study.

The study is seeking participants who are:

* adults, 18 to 70 years of age (inclusive)
* have a body mass index (BMI) equal to, or more than 25 kilograms/meter square (kg/m2) up to 40 kg/m2.
* limited mild, stable long-term medical conditions are allowed as assessed by the study doctor.

People who want to join the study will first go through a screening period of up to 4 weeks. The study will look at how the study medicine is tolerated, including whether participants have any reactions. It will assess how they feel after receiving multiple doses. It will also measure the amounts of study medicine in the blood and urine over time.

Participants will take part in this study for about 24 to 40 weeks including treatment and follow-up period after the final dose. Treatment duration may vary depending on their assigned group.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Treatment Emergent Adverse Events (TEAEs)
title: A Study to Learn How Different Amounts of the Study Medicine Called PF-08656795 Are Tolerated and Act in Adults With Overweight or Obesity

brief_summary: This is a single-arm, multicenter Phase III clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of prophylactic treatment with SR604 Injection in hemophilia A/B patients with or without inhibitors.
lead_sponsor: Shanghai RAAS Blood Products Co., Ltd.
primary_outcomes: Treated total annualized bleeding rate (ABR) over 28 weeks of treatment
title: A Phase III Clinical Trial Evaluating SR604 Injection for Prophylactic Treatment in Patients With Hemophilia

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether \[18F\]AlF-FAPI-74 PET/CT can help detect endometriosis in adult women who are already scheduled for laparoscopy due to suspicion of deep infiltrating endometriosis or superficial peritoneal endometriosis. The main aims are: (i) How well does \[18F\]AlF-FAPI-74 PET/CT identify endometriosis lesions compared with findings during laparoscopy? (ii) Can PET/CT identify additional lesions that may not be seen on ultrasound or MRI? (iii) Can ultra-high-resolution NeuroEXPLORER PET/CT improve the detection of small lesions compared with standard PET/CT? Participants will: (i) Receive an intravenous injection of \[18F\]AlF-FAPI-74 followed by a PET/CT scan before their planned laparoscopy. (ii) Undergo their planned laparoscopy, during which PET findings will be compared with the surgical findings and where tissue is removed with laboratory analysis. (iii) Optionally undergo an additional NeuroEXPLORER PET/CT scan after the same tracer injection. (iv) Optionally undergo a second \[18F\]AlF-FAPI-74 PET/CT if participants started gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) treatment after their first scan to investigate whether tracer uptake in endometriosis lesions changes during treatment.
primary_outcomes: Evaluate diagnostic performance of [18F]AlF-FAPI-74 PET/CT as a non-invasive tool to diagnose deep infiltrating endometriosis and/or superficial peritoneal endometriosis, in comparison with laparoscopic findings in women with suspected endometriosis
Frequency of serious adverse device effects (SADEs) related to NeuroEXPLORER PET/CT
title: Prospective Trial of [18F]AlF-FAPI-74 for PET Imaging of Fibroblast Activation Protein in Patients With Endometriosis

brief_summary:
The goal of the study is to investigate the effects of carbohydrate counting training-administered to pediatric patients diagnosed with GSD 1a and 1b-on blood glucose regulation, quality of life, urinary glucotetrasaccharide (Glc4) levels, and various biomarkers. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is there a significant change in the urinary Glc4 parameter of patients diagnosed with GSD1 who employ the carbohydrate counting method?
* Does the implementation of the carbohydrate counting method in the diets of patients diagnosed with GSD1 lead to a significant change in their quality of life?
* Is there a significant change in the HbA1c (%) levels of patients diagnosed with GSD1 who practice the carbohydrate counting method?
* Does the application of the carbohydrate counting method in the diets of patients diagnosed with GSD1 result in a significant change in the frequency of infections?

Children aged 2-18 years diagnosed with GSD1 will be monitored for a period of 3 months; during this time, food consumption records and anthropometric measurements will be collected, retrospective analysis of continuous glucose monitoring sensor(CGMS) data will be conducted, and various questionnaires and rating scales will be completed both online and in person.
primary_outcomes: Changes in blood glucose regulation among individuals who have received carbohydrate counting training, compared to baseline values.
Changes in urinary Glc4 levels in individuals who received carbohydrate counting training compared to baseline values.
Change in quality of life scale scores of individuals who received carbohydrate counting training, relative to baseline values.
Change in HbA1c (%) value compared to baseline
title: Effects of the Carbohydrate Counting Method on Blood Glucose Regulation, Quality of Life, Urinary Glc4 and Other Biomarkers in Children With GSD1

brief_summary:
Aim of the study This study aims to evaluate the effect of a nurse-led menopause self-management box on hot flash frequency and menopause-specific quality of life among postmenopausal women.

Research hypotheses

* Postmenopausal women who receive the nurse-led menopause self-management box will demonstrate significantly lower mean daily hot flash frequency immediately after the four-week intervention and at the three-month follow-up compared with baseline.
* Postmenopausal women who receive the intervention will demonstrate significantly lower hot flash severity immediately after the four-week intervention and at the three-month follow-up compared with baseline.
* Postmenopausal women who receive the intervention will demonstrate significantly lower MENQOL scores, indicating improved menopause-specific quality of life, immediately after the four-week intervention and at the three-month follow-up compared with baseline.
interventions: Components of Nurse-Led Menopause Self- Management Box
primary_outcomes: Hot Flash Frequency and Menopause-Specific Quality of Life
title: Self-Management Box on Hot Flash in Postmenopausal Women

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether rinsing the egg sacs (follicles) during egg collection helps doctors collect more eggs in women with low egg reserve. Participants are unmarried women aged 18 to 42 who are freezing their eggs and who chose to have eggs collected through the abdomen instead of the vagina. Low egg reserve means a blood level of anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) of 1 ng/mL or lower.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does rinsing the follicles raise the total number of eggs collected? Does rinsing the follicles raise the number of mature eggs that can be frozen?

Researchers will compare two egg collection methods, each used routinely at one of two IVF centres in Turkey:

Direct aspiration: each follicle is emptied once with a single-channel needle, with no rinsing.

Follicular flushing: a double-channel needle is used. If no egg is found after the first try, the follicle is rinsed with warm fluid and emptied again, up to six times.

Participants will:

Take fertility hormone injections for about 8 to 12 days so that several follicles grow Have their eggs collected through the abdomen under sedation, guided by ultrasound Have their mature eggs frozen for future use
primary_outcomes: Number of Metaphase II (MII) Oocytes Retrieved per Participant
title: Follicular Flushing Versus Direct Aspiration in Transabdominal Oocyte Retrieval

brief_summary: METH-RENAL is a prospective observational diagnostic development and threshold-setting study in adults with a renal mass scheduled for partial or radical nephrectomy. Peripheral blood is collected before surgery, and postoperative histopathology serves as the reference standard. The study will develop and internally validate a plasma DNA methylation classifier and lock the final marker panel, algorithm, and positivity cut-off for a subsequent independent prospective multicenter validation study.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic performance of the final plasma DNA methylation classifier
title: Plasma DNA Methylation for Preoperative Classification of Renal Masses

brief_summary: This exploratory clinical imaging study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, biodistribution, lesion detection, and tumor uptake characteristics of 68Ga- and 18F-labeled carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX)-targeted positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) in patients with renal tumors or suspected renal cell carcinoma. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either 68Ga-CAIX or 18F-CAIX PET/CT. All participants will also undergo 18F-FDG PET/CT for comparison. The study will further explore the association between CAIX-targeted PET findings and CAIX expression assessed by immunohistochemistry, as well as the diagnostic performance of CAIX-targeted PET/CT for lesion detection.
primary_outcomes: Semiquantitative Uptake of CAIX-Targeted Tracers
title: 68Ga- and 18F-CAIX PET Imaging Study

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effect of a compassion-based intervention compared with standard procedure for rehabilitation needs assessment among patients undergoing surgery for colorectal cancer with curative intent.

Participants were randomly assigned to either a structured, compassion-supported rehabilitation needs assessment or standard postoperative care. The intervention focused on identifying physical, psychological, and social rehabilitation needs through compassionate communication and facilitating referral to municipal cancer rehabilitation services.

The primary outcome was health-related quality of life measured using the Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy-Colorectal (FACT-C) at three months. Secondary outcomes included anxiety, depression, self-compassion, and participation in cancer rehabilitation.
lead_sponsor: Esbjerg Hospital - University Hospital of Southern Denmark
primary_outcomes: Health-Related Quality of Life Measured by FACT-C Total Score
title: Compassion-Based Rehabilitation Needs Assessment Following Colorectal Cancer Surgery

brief_summary: This randomized controlled study evaluated the effects of an eight-week progressive muscle relaxation program on anxiety, depression, and quality of life in 80 adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Participants were randomly assigned to the intervention group (n = 40) or the control group (n = 40). The intervention included individual training lasting approximately 30-40 minutes, an educational booklet, relaxation audio recordings for home practice, and weekly telephone follow-up. Participants were instructed to practise the exercises every morning for eight weeks. The control group received no study-specific relaxation intervention. Anxiety, depression, and quality of life were assessed at baseline and at week eight. A subsequent qualitative component involved in-depth interviews with 10 participants to explore their experiences with the program.
primary_outcomes: Change in Diabetes-Related Quality of Life Score from Baseline to Week 8
title: Effects of Progressive Muscle Relaxation on Anxiety, Depression, and Quality of Life in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of combining low-dose radiotherapy to the intestines with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in patients with liver metastases from solid tumors.

Liver metastases often create an "immune desert" that makes immunotherapy less effective. Recent research has shown that low-dose irradiation of the gut (1 Gy) can reshape the gut microbiome and activate the immune system, potentially reversing resistance to immunotherapy.

This is a prospective, single-arm, single-center cohort study. We plan to enroll 120 patients with liver metastases from non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), colorectal cancer, or pancreatic cancer. All participants will receive a single low dose of radiotherapy to the intestine (1 Gy), followed by standard immune checkpoint inhibitors and chemotherapy.

The main goal of this study is to see how well the liver metastases respond to this combined treatment. We will also monitor survival, side effects, and changes in the gut bacteria and blood immune markers to understand how this treatment works. This strategy may provide a low-cost, low-toxicity new option for patients whose liver metastases have stopped responding to standard immunotherapy.
primary_outcomes: Objective Response Rate (ORR) of Liver Metastases
title: Intestinal Low-Dose Radiotherapy Combined With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Solid Tumors With Liver Metastases

brief_summary:
X-linked myotubular myopathy (XLMTM) is a rare and serious condition present at birth where the muscles do not work properly. There are currently no approved therapies for XLMTM.

The protein myotubularin is needed for muscle development, movement and breathing. A gene called MTM1 tells the body to make myotubularin. XLMTM is caused by changes, or mutations, in the MTM1 gene. Changes in the MTM1 gene cause low or no levels of myotubularin to be made, so the muscles do not work properly.

Gene therapy is a way of getting a healthy copy of a gene into the body. This allows the body's cells to make a normal protein that may reduce disease symptoms. Researchers have developed ASP2957 to get a healthy MTM1 gene into the body. This could help improve muscle development and function in young children with XLMTM.

A single dose of ASP2957 has previously been given to young boys in an earlier study, but health authorities require up to a 5-year follow-up of the boys. This study is a long-term follow-up study of the young boys with XLMTM who previously received ASP2957 in an earlier study. They won't receive ASP2957 in this long-term study.

The main aims of the study is recording medical problems that happen during this study after receiving ASP2957 (in the earlier study), and whether they were caused by ASP2957 or not. This may include abnormal results from blood tests, medical examinations and imaging to check heart health.

They may continue to take medicines that lower their immune system from an earlier study. These help to avoid a reaction to ASP2957.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs)
Number of participants with serious adverse events (SAEs)
Number of participants with adverse events of special interest (AESIs)
title: A Long-term Follow-up Study in Male Participants With X-linked Myotubular Myopathy Treated With ASP2957

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled clinical trial aims to compare the clinical performance of CAD/CAM lithium disilicate (IPS e.max CAD) and 3D-printed resin (BEGO VarseoSmile TriniQ) endocrown restorations in endodontically treated posterior teeth.

Eligible patients requiring indirect restorations of two posterior teeth will receive both types of endocrown restorations using a randomized design. All restorations will be fabricated using standardized digital workflows and adhesive cementation protocols.

Clinical evaluations will be performed at one week, six months, and one year following restoration placement. The functional, esthetic, and biological properties of the restorations will be assessed according to the World Dental Federation (FDI) criteria. Periapical radiographs will be obtained to evaluate endodontic outcomes.

The study aims to compare the clinical survival, functional performance, and potential complications of the two restorative materials, including restoration fracture, debonding, and secondary caries.
conditions: Restoration of Endodontically Treated Posterior Teeth
interventions: IPS e.max CAD Lithium Disilicate Endocrown
primary_outcomes: Clinical Performance of Endocrown Restorations According to FDI Criteria
title: Clinical Comparison of Lithium Disilicate and 3D-Printed Resin Endocrowns

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a coffee pulp infusion works to improve muscle recovery after moderate physical exercise in a healthy adult population. It will also learn about its effects on oxidative stress and inflammation caused by exercise according to sex. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the coffee pulp infusion reduce the levels of oxidative stress, inflammation, and muscle damage markers after physical activity?
* Are there differences between men and women regarding the response to the exercise and the benefits of the infusion? Researchers will compare the coffee pulp infusion to a placebo (a wheat bran infusion equalized in appearance and flavor but with low bioactive potential) to see if the coffee pulp infusion works to improve muscle recovery.

Participants will:

* Take the coffee pulp infusion or the placebo twice every day for 45 consecutive days.
* Complete a total of 6 clinic and sports center appointments for physical tests, anthropometric records, and hemodynamic monitoring.
* Perform a leg extension exercise protocol specifically calibrated to induce muscle stress and fatigue.
* Provide capillary blood and morning urine samples at specific time points to measure biomarkers and metabolomic responses.
* Complete several questionnaires regarding their sociodemographics, physical activity, dietary index, and perceived muscle soreness or effort.
interventions: Two 250 mL infusions per day (one in the morning and one at night) for 45 consecutive days.
primary_outcomes: Change in Plasma Biomarkers of Skeletal Muscle Damage.
title: Development of a Coffee Pulp Infusion as a Strategy for Recovery After Moderate Physical Exercise in a Healthy Population.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to find out whether a new taekwondo-specific field test (TSFT) is a valid way to measure the fitness of taekwondo athletes. The TSFT was designed to reflect what athletes actually do in competition: repeated, high-intensity kicks scored by an official electronic scoring system, with short rest periods in between.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

* Is performance on the TSFT related to aerobic fitness (estimated VO2max) measured with the 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test?
* Is performance on the TSFT related to anaerobic performance and fatigue tolerance measured with the Wingate Anaerobic Test?

Male sub-elite taekwondo athletes completed the new TSFT and two widely used reference tests (the 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test and the Wingate Anaerobic Test). Researchers then compared the results of the new test with those of the reference tests.
primary_outcomes: Taekwondo-Specific Field Test (TSFT) Mean Points
Estimated Maximal Oxygen Uptake (VO2max) From the 30-15 Intermittent Fitness Test
title: Validity of a New Taekwondo-Specific Field Test in Sub-Elite Athletes

brief_summary: This is a first-in-human, Phase 1, open-label study evaluating MTX-531, an investigational dual EGFR/PI3K inhibitor, in adults with advanced solid tumors. The study will evaluate the safety and tolerability of MTX-531, determine the maximum tolerated dose and recommended Phase 2 dose, and assess how the drug is processed by the body and its preliminary anti-tumor activity.
conditions: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
primary_outcomes: Safety and Tolerability profile of MTX-531
Provisional RP2D For Further Evaluation of MTX-531
title: MTX-531-001 Phase 1 Study in Advanced Solid Tumors

brief_summary: This randomized, single-blind, controlled clinical trial aims to evaluate the effects of a topical curcumin spray on post-extraction wound healing and postoperative symptoms in adults undergoing first molar extraction. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: curcumin topical spray, 0.12% chlorhexidine topical spray, or standard postoperative care without a topical spray. The interventions will be applied twice daily for 7 days. Postoperative pain will be assessed using a visual analog scale, while wound healing will be evaluated using the Landry, Turnbull, and Howley Healing Index. Wound dimensions will also be recorded during follow-up. In addition, salivary levels of inflammatory biomarkers, including interleukin-1β (IL-1β), tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), will be analyzed to assess the local inflammatory response during the postoperative healing period.The study aims to compare the clinical effects of topical curcumin with chlorhexidine and standard postoperative care during the early healing period after tooth extraction.
primary_outcomes: Extraction Socket Healing Assessed Using the Landry, Turnbull and Howley Healing Index
title: Effect of Curcumin Topical Spray on Wound Healing After Tooth Extraction

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if cryoneurolysis, a targeted cold therapy applied to nerve branches, can relax the muscles of the abdomen to facilitate surgical repair of abdominal wall hernias. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does cryoneurolysis result in changes to the length of the abdominal oblique muscles and hernia size?
* Are there any side effects with the procedure?
* What are the rates of complete hernia closure and component separation at the time of hernia repair?

Participants will

* Undergo cryoneurolysis procedure between two to six weeks prior to scheduled hernia repair
* Complete a telephone visit 24-48 hours after the procedure to review any side effects
* Undergo repeat computed tomography (CT) scan one to two weeks after the procedure to detect changes to the abdominal muscles and hernia size
* Undergo routine postoperative clinic visits including 30 days after hernia repair surgery
primary_outcomes: Change from baseline in Computed Tomography (CT) measured length of oblique muscles and hernia defect size in centimeters
title: Cryoneurolysis for Abdominal Wall Relaxation Prior to Ventral Hernia Repair

brief_summary: This single-center, prospective, randomized, controlled, assessor-blinded study will evaluate the efficacy and safety of Piclosept® ophthalmic solution as an adjunct to standardized lacrimal sac massage in children aged 1 to 12 months with neonatal dacryocystitis. Participants will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to standardized lacrimal sac massage alone, massage plus preservative-free levofloxacin, or massage plus Piclosept®. The primary outcome is clinical success on Day 14, defined as complete absence of purulent-mucoid discharge and reflux of purulent-mucoid material.
primary_outcomes: Resolution of congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction
Clinical success at Day 14
title: Efficacy and Safety of Piclosept in the Complex Treatment of Neonatal Dacryocystitis

brief_summary: This study aims to improve our understanding of how people with knee osteoarthritis think about, regulate, and adapt their physical activity while participating in Joint Academy's digital osteoarthritis programme for knee osteoarthritis. The study will investigate how understanding of the regulation of physical activity, psychological factors, and patterns of daily activity are related to participation in rehabilitation and changes in physical function over time. By gaining a better understanding of how people experience and manage physical activity in the context of knee osteoarthritis, we hope to improve the knee osteoarthritis programme and support rehabilitation that is better tailored to individual needs.
primary_outcomes: Patient Specific Functional Scale
KOOS-12 Function subscale
title: Person-Centred Digital Rehabilitation for Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether Stanford Accelerated Intelligent Neuromodulation Therapy (SAINT®), a type of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), is safe and may improve memory and thinking in adults aged 65 or older with treatment-resistant depression and memory concerns. Researchers will also study whether SAINT® improves depression symptoms.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does SAINT® improve memory and thinking five days after treatment?
* Does SAINT® improve depression symptoms and overall well-being?
* Do changes in memory, mood, or daily activities last for up to one year?
* What side effects or safety concerns occur during and after treatment?

All participants will receive SAINT® treatment. There is no placebo group.

Participants will:

* Complete memory, mood, and health assessments and have an MRI scan
* Receive 10 TMS sessions each day for 5 days in a row
* Return for follow-up visits for up to 12 months

Researchers will track changes in memory, mood, daily activities, and side effects.
interventions: Stanford Accelerated Intelligent Neuromodulation Therapy (SAINT®) with the Magnus Neuromodulation System
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) Score at 5 Days Post-Stimulation
title: SAINT® Therapy for Memory Problems in Older Adults With Treatment-Resistant Depression

brief_summary:
This trial is being done in non-obese healthy participants to compare two different forms of cenvacibart.

The main goal of the trial is to learn about the trial medicine and how it is absorbed, modified, and removed from the body.

The trial will look at:

* What side effects cenvacibart might cause and how it feels after the dose
* Levels of cenvacibart in the blood at different time points
* Whether the body makes proteins called antibodies against cenvacibart (which could make the trial medicine less effective or could lead to side effects)
* What happens when cenvacibart travels through the body
primary_outcomes: Area under the concentration-time curve from time zero to the last quantifiable concentration (AUClast)
Maximum observed concentration (Cmax)
title: Healthy Adult Participants Trial Comparing Different Cenvacibart Presentations

brief_summary:
This study aimed to evaluate the effects of the 4-7-8 breathing technique performed before colonoscopy on patients' anxiety, pain, and embarrassment. Colonoscopy is a procedure used to examine the inside of the large intestine and may cause anxiety, discomfort, and embarrassment in some patients.

In this randomized controlled study, 104 patients undergoing colonoscopy were assigned to either an intervention group or a control group. Patients in the intervention group performed the 4-7-8 breathing technique before colonoscopy, while patients in the control group received usual care. Anxiety, pain, and embarrassment were assessed to compare outcomes between the two groups.

This study aimed to evaluate the effects of the 4-7-8 breathing technique performed before colonoscopy on patients' anxiety levels, pain intensity, feelings of embarrassment, and physiological parameters.
primary_outcomes: Anxiety Level (State Anxiety Inventory Score)
title: 4-7-8 Breathing Before Colonoscopy: Effects on Anxiety, Pain, and Embarrassment

brief_summary:
Obesity adversely affects respiratory physiology by reducing lung volumes and compliance and increasing airway resistance and alveolar collapse. These effects are further aggravated by pneumoperitoneum during laparoscopic surgery, increasing the risk of impaired oxygenation and ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI).

Mechanical power (MP) reflects the total energy transferred to the respiratory system during mechanical ventilation and is influenced by tidal volume, respiratory rate, airway pressures, flow, and PEEP. Increased airway and driving pressures may contribute to higher mechanical power and lung injury, particularly in obese patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery.

This study aims to compare flow-controlled ventilation (FCV) and volume-controlled ventilation with autoflow (VC-AF) in obese patients undergoing laparoscopic surgery in terms of airway pressures, driving pressure, and mechanical power. The investigators hypothesize that FCV may reduce airway pressures, driving pressure, and mechanical power compared with VC-AF, potentially decreasing the risk of VILI. The effect of FCV on oxygenation will also be evaluated as a secondary outcome.
primary_outcomes: Mechanical Power (J/min)
Driving Pressure (cmH₂O)
Plateau Airway Pressure (cmH₂O)
Peak Airway Pressure (cmH₂O)
title: VC-AF vs FCV in Obese Patients Undergoing Laparoscopic Surgery

brief_summary: Peroral endoscopic esophageal myotomy (POEM) has been established as an effective therapy for Achalasia. It is still not known how deep the myotomy should be and if it should include the circular and longitudinal muscles or not. It is hypothesized that a complete full thickness myotomy could lead to higher rates of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). In this study we compare performing a Full-thickness myotomy with a progressive myotomy (proximal half circular only, distal half full-thickness, and assessment the different outcomes including efficacy and the incidence of postprocedural GERD.
primary_outcomes: Presence of Esophagitis
title: Full-thickness Versus Progressive Myotomy in Peroral Endoscopic Esophageal Myotomy in Achalasia: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: This prospective study evaluates the impact of video-based patient education compared to standard verbal informed consent on state anxiety levels and procedure acceptance rates in pregnant women undergoing invasive prenatal diagnostic testing (amniocentesis or chorionic villus sampling). Participants are assigned to four groups based on their video preference and procedural recommendation to assess changes in anxiety scores (STAI-S) before and after counseling, as well as final decisions regarding the procedure.
primary_outcomes: Change in Maternal State Anxiety Level
Procedure Acceptance Rate
title: Effect of Video -Based vs Standard ınformation on Maternal Anxiety and Procedure Decision in Pregnant Woman Offered Amniocentesis or Cvs

brief_summary: This study is a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study that evaluates the safety and tolerability of a fiber-based dietary supplement and the mechanistic and structure-function effects of that supplement on the gut and vaginal microbiome, gastrointestinal well-being, and quality-of-life parameters in 140 women with endometriosis and co-existing gastrointestinal symptoms over 12 weeks. The primary objective is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of the supplement, measured by the incidence and severity of gastrointestinal adverse events (AEs) and discontinuations. Secondary objectives include assessing the fibers impact on gastrointestinal symptoms and quality of life through the use of custom questionnaires built for the study population and evaluation of other endometriosis related parameters such as pelvic discomfort. Exploratory objectives focus on the exploration of the gut and vaginal microbiomes, their connection to endometriosis, and how they are impacted by the study product.
primary_outcomes: Incidence and severity of GI adverse events (AEs) and discontinuations.
title: Evaluating the Impact of a Multi-Fiber Prebiotic Dietary Supplement (LOAM) in Women With Endometriosis and Co-existing Gastrointestinal Symptoms

brief_summary: This is a single-arm, single-center clinical study to assess the efficacy and safety of Mitoxantrone Hydrochloride Liposome combined with cladribine and sotoraclib in patients with relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia (R/R-AML). Eligible adult participants will receive the following regimen: Mitoxantrone Hydrochloride Liposome 20 mg/m²; cladribine 5 mg/m² on day 1-5; sotoraclib 20 mg on day1, 40 mg on day2, 80 mg on day3, 160 mg on day4-day9. Clinical efficacy endpoints include overall response rate. Safety will be assessed via adverse event monitoring and laboratory examinations. All subjects will be followed up for survival and relapse status.
conditions: Relapsed and Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia (RR-AML)
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated People's Hospital of Ningbo University
primary_outcomes: Overall Response Rate (ORR)
title: Mitoxantrone Hydrochloride Liposome Combined With Cladribine And Sotorasib For Relapsed Refractory Acute Myeloid Leukemia

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare the acute effects of virtual reality exergames (VR-EXG) and spinal manipulation on pain, kinesiophobia, mood states, functional disability and lumbar range of motion in individuals with chronic nonspecific low back pain.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a single session of VR-EXG affect pain, kinesiophobia, mood states, functional disability and lumbar range of motion in individuals with chronic nonspecific low back pain?
* Does a single session of spinal manipulation affect pain, kinesiophobia, mood states, functional disability and lumbar range of motion in individuals with chronic nonspecific low back pain?
* Is there a difference between VR-EXG and spinal manipulation in their acute effects on pain, kinesiophobia, mood states, functional disability and lumbar range of motion?

Researchers will compare participants receiving VR-EXG with those receiving spinal manipulation to determine whether one intervention produces greater acute improvements in pain, kinesiophobia, mood states, functional disability and lumbar range of motion.

Participants will be divided into two groups to be compared: the first group will receive virtual reality exergaming (VR-EXG), while the second group will receive spinal manipulation.
primary_outcomes: Pain intensity measured using the visual analogue Scale (VAS)
title: Effects of Virtual Reality Exergames Versus Spinal Manipulation in Chronic Nonspecific Low Back Pain

brief_summary: Factor X deficiency is one of the most severe rare bleeding disorders and may lead to serious spontaneous hemorrhages, particularly in patients with severe congenital forms. Acquired FX deficiency is even rarer, most frequently associated with AL amyloidosis, and remains poorly characterized. Establishing a comprehensive patient registry is essential to improve understanding of disease epidemiology, clinical manifestations, and treatment outcomes, ultimately supporting evidence-based management strategies.
primary_outcomes: Bleedings
title: A Database For The Collection Of Clinical, Laboratory, And Treatment Data From Patients With Factor X Deficiency To Define The Natural History Of The Disease And Improve Patient Management

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial investigates whether two time-efficient forms of high-intensity exercise, high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and exercise snacking, improve glycemic control, cardiorespiratory fitness and other cardiometabolic risk factors in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Over 12 weeks, participants were allocated to HIIT, exercise snacking, or a non-exercise control group. The study addresses two questions: whether each exercise modality improves these outcomes relative to no exercise, and whether accumulating vigorous exercise in brief bouts throughout the day produces adaptations comparable to those of conventional interval training performed in a single session.
primary_outcomes: Change in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c)
Change in fasting blood glucose (FBG)
Change in estimated relative peak oxygen uptake (VO₂peak)
Change in estimated absolute peak oxygen uptake (VO₂peak)
title: Effects of High-Intensity Interval Training and Exercise Snacking on Glycemic Control and Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus

brief_summary: The effect of deksmedetomidine infusion on ischemia-reperfusion injury related to tourniquet application during total knee replacement will be evaluated by malondialdehyde and total antioksidant status.
lead_sponsor: Diskapi Yildirim Beyazit Education and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: blood malondialdehide levels
blood malondialdehide levels
blood malondialdehide levels
blood total antioksidant status
blood total antioksidant status
blood total antioksidant status
title: Dexmedetomidine Infusion and Iscemia and Reperfusion Injury

brief_summary: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder affecting women of reproductive age and is associated with obesity, insulin resistance, poor physical fitness, and reduced quality of life. This randomized controlled trial will examine how High intensity Interval Training (HIIT) and Mat Pilates effect body composition, physical fitness, and quality of life in women diagnosed with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) . A total of 60 participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups; HIIT, Mat Pilates, or a control group. Each intervention will run for eight weeks, with body composition, physical fitness, and quality of life measured both before and after the program to evaluate the comparative effectiveness of the two exercise intervention.
primary_outcomes: Change in Body Composition
Body circumference
Change in Skinfold Thickness
title: High Intensity Interval Training Versus Mat Pilates in Women With PCOS

brief_summary:
Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is commonly associated with significant postoperative pain, including pain arising from the posterior aspect of the knee. Regional anesthesia techniques are frequently used as part of a multimodal analgesic strategy to improve pain control, reduce opioid requirements, and facilitate early functional recovery.

This prospective, randomized, double-blind, superiority clinical trial will compare the analgesic efficacy of the interspace between the popliteal artery and capsule of the posterior knee (iPACK) block with the popliteal plexus block in adult patients undergoing elective unilateral primary total knee arthroplasty. All participants will receive a continuous femoral triangle block and a standardized multimodal postoperative analgesic regimen.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either an ultrasound-guided iPACK block or an ultrasound-guided popliteal plexus block. The primary outcome will be cumulative intravenous morphine consumption delivered through a patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) device during the first 24 hours after surgery.

Secondary outcomes will include cumulative morphine consumption during the first 12 hours, posterior knee pain at rest and during movement, time to first PCA morphine administration, quality of recovery assessed with the QoR-15 questionnaire, distal motor function, early functional recovery, block performance time, postoperative adverse effects, and neurological symptoms.

The study hypothesis is that the popliteal plexus block will provide superior opioid-sparing analgesia compared with the iPACK block when both techniques are combined with a continuous femoral triangle block, while preserving distal motor function and maintaining an acceptable safety profile.
primary_outcomes: Cumulative Intravenous Morphine Equivalent Consumption During the First 24 Hours After Surgery.
title: A Randomized Comparison of the Efficacy of the IPACK Block Versus the Popliteal Plexus Block for Posterior Knee Analgesia, in Patients Undergoing a Total Knee Arthroplasty and Receiving a Continuous Distal Femoral Triangle Block

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate whether metabolic and inflammatory indices differ between patients with chronic lateral epicondylitis (tennis elbow) and individuals without the condition. It will also examine whether these indices are associated with pain severity and functional limitations in patients with lateral epicondylitis.

This observational, controlled cross-sectional study will include 144 participants aged 30-65 years: 72 patients with chronic lateral epicondylitis and 72 controls without lateral epicondylitis.

Metabolic and inflammatory indices will be calculated using laboratory test results obtained on the day of study enrollment as part of routine clinical care. These include fasting glucose, triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, and monocyte count. The main index will be the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index. Additional indices will include the atherogenic index of plasma (AIP), monocyte-to-HDL cholesterol ratio (MHR), and triglyceride-glucose body mass index (TyG-BMI).

Pain severity and functional limitations will be assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and the Patient-Rated Tennis Elbow Evaluation (PRTEE) in patients with lateral epicondylitis. Demographic characteristics, smoking status, and occupational physical demands will also be recorded.
primary_outcomes: Difference in Triglyceride-Glucose (TyG) Index Between Groups
title: Metabolic and Inflammatory Indices in Lateral Epicondylitis

brief_summary:
This study compares two approaches to starting walking and weight bearing after surgery for a fracture near the hip in older adults. All participants undergo fixation with a dynamic hip screw, a metal implant that holds the broken bone in position while it heals.

Ninety participants are randomly assigned to two equal groups. One group starts weight bearing during the first week after surgery. The other group delays mobilization until after the first week. Both groups receive routine postoperative care and physiotherapy.

The study aims to determine whether earlier weight bearing improves pain, walking ability, and everyday activities. Recovery is assessed using the Modified Harris Hip Score at six weeks and three months after surgery. Postoperative complications are also recorded.
primary_outcomes: Modified Harris Hip Score
title: DHS Fixation for Extra Capsular Fractures of Proximal Femur in Geriatric Population

brief_summary:
Periapical radiographs of dental implants, acquired as part of two ongoing research projects, will be retrospectively analyzed using a newly developed image quality scoring form. Following an initial classification (Excellent - Acceptable - Rejected), a detailed assessment of the various image quality criteria and any deviations from these criteria will be performed. In addition, the frequency with which radiographs had to be retaken to obtain a diagnostically acceptable image will be evaluated. The influence of anatomical factors (e.g., implant location in the mouth, maxilla or mandible, etc.) and the use of individualized radiographic holders will also be assessed.

Through this retrospective analysis of an existing dataset of implant radiographs, the study aims to identify the factors that have influenced image quality, the ability to accurately assess the surrounding bone level, and the need for repeat radiographic exposures. The findings may contribute to the development of guidelines to improve the quality of periapical radiographs and potentially reduce radiation exposure for patients.
primary_outcomes: Rejection classification
Repeat rate
Interexaminer reproducibility of the reject analysis.
Intra-examiner reproducibility
title: Reject Analysis of Periapical Radiographs of Dental Implants.

brief_summary: This is a single-center, open-label, dose-escalation, investigator-initiated pilot study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, dose-limiting toxicity (DLT), and pharmacodynamic signals of orelabrutinib in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). A 12-week run-in observation period will be used to establish each participant's historical ALSFRS-R decline slope. Participants will receive orelabrutinib 50 mg once daily (QD), 100 mg QD, or optional 150 mg QD using a 3+3 dose-escalation design for 24 weeks, followed by a 4-week safety follow-up.
primary_outcomes: Serious adverse event (SAE) incidence
Adverse event (AE) incidence and severity
Dose-limiting toxicity (DLT)
Number of subjects who discontinue treatment prematurely
Number of patients who discontinue treatment prematurely due to adverse events

Number of patients with clinically significant abnormal laboratory and ancillary examinations (including routine laboratory tests, cardiac safety, infection markers, bleeding markers, and new-onset tumor examinations)
title: Safety, Tolerability, and Pharmacodynamic Exploration of Orelabrutinib in Patients With Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

brief_summary: This is a single-center, single-arm, exploratory clinical study evaluating the efficacy and safety of MRG003 (Becotatug Vedotin) in patients with relapsed small cell lung cancer. Eligible patients receive becotatug vedotin at a dose of 2.3 mg/kg administered by intravenous infusion once every 21 days until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. The primary endpoint is overall survival (OS). Secondary endpoints include progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and safety.
primary_outcomes: Overall Survival (OS)
title: Effectiveness and Safety of MRG003 (Becotatug Vedotin) in Relapsed SCLC

brief_summary:
The goal of this basic neuroscience study is to learn whether visual feedback of brain activity can help improve arm and hand recovery in people who recently had a stroke. The study will also examine whether this type of training is practical to use during early stroke rehabilitation. Researchers will compare two groups of participants. Both groups will practice reaching for and grasping a cup, either by physically performing the movement or imagining the movement. One group will receive visual feedback showing their brain activity during practice. The other group will complete the same practice without seeing this feedback. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of these groups.

The study will include 60 participants who had a stroke and who have weakness in one arm. Participants will complete 8 in-person sessions over 2 weeks. The first and last sessions will include tests of arm function, disability, quality of life, and brain activity. The 6 sessions in between will involve repeated movement or imagined movement practice. During the sessions, researchers will use functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), a non-invasive brain imaging tool that shines light into the scalp to measure changes in brain activity. Small sensors placed on the skin of the arm and hand will also be used to measure muscle activity.
primary_outcomes: functional Near Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) amplitude over the motor cortex
title: Enabling Bedside Brain Measurement of Motor Outcomes Post Stroke

brief_summary: This observational study aims to validate whether a novel wearable sensor can non-invasively and remotely assess the renal health status of patients with diabetes by detecting the concentration of ammonia (NH₃) in exhaled breath, thereby facilitating the early detection and diagnosis of diabetic kidney disease (DKD). The study will enroll approximately 2,000 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, employing a single breath sample collection combined with conventional renal function tests to establish a predictive model linking exhaled ammonia concentration with kidney disease stage, and to validate its diagnostic accuracy.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Performance of Breath Ammonia Concentration for Diabetic Kidney Disease Staging
Performance of the Wearable NH₃ Sensor
title: Wearable NH₃ Sensor for Remote Non-invasive Monitoring and Diagnosis of Diabetic Kidney Disease

brief_summary:
Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two clinical treatment Arms, both of which are standard care procedures performed in the right atrium (RA):

Arm A: Pacing from the Bachmann's Bundle (BB) in the right atrium (upper right chamber of the heart) Arm B: Pacing from the right atrial appendage (RAA - a sac attached to the right atrium) Neither of these treatments are experimental; both are routinely performed by Electrophysiologists in the clinical setting. The purpose of this study is to compare side by side these two treatments and evaluate if one is better than the other. After the procedure, participants will be followed for one year.

Medical record data will be collected, and a blood sample will be collected upon enrollment and at one year after implantation. Research-related surveys will be completed at the standard-care 3-, 6-, and 12-month visits.
lead_sponsor: Allegheny Singer Research Institute (also known as Allegheny Health Network Research Institute)
primary_outcomes: Cardiac Procedural Outcomes
title: Bachmann's Bundle Versus Right Atrial Appendage Pacing

brief_summary: This randomized, triple-blinded, counterbalanced crossover trial compared three carbohydrate beverages that provided the same amount of carbohydrate (30 g) but differed in carbohydrate source: dextrose, maltodextrin, and highly branched cyclic dextrin (HBCD). Resistance-trained adults completed a familiarization session, a one-repetition maximum (1RM) testing session, and three experimental sessions separated by at least 7 days. In each experimental session, participants ingested one of the beverages in three 10-g servings and performed five sets of up to 15 repetitions at 62.5% of 1RM in the squat, bench press, and bench pull. Mechanical performance, blood glucose and lactate, perceived exertion, and gastrointestinal symptoms were assessed during or immediately after exercise; perceived recovery and muscle soreness at 24 and 48 hours; and serum creatine kinase and cortisol at 48 hours.
primary_outcomes: Fastest Mean Concentric Velocity per Set (MVfastest)
title: Effects of Three Carbohydrate Beverages on Resistance Training Performance

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled Phase IV clinical trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of sitogilun malate tablets in combination with amlodipine besylate tablets in patients with mild to moderate essential hypertension and risk of early kidney damage. Approximately 456 eligible participants will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive sitogilun malate plus amlodipine, allisartan isoproxil plus amlodipine, or placebo plus amlodipine for 8 weeks. The primary efficacy outcome is the change from baseline in mean sitting diastolic blood pressure (msDBP) at Week 8. Secondary efficacy outcomes include changes in mean sitting systolic blood pressure (msSBP), blood pressure response and control rates, ambulatory blood pressure parameters, and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR). Safety will also be evaluated throughout the study.
lead_sponsor: Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Mean Sitting Diastolic Blood Pressure (msDBP) at Week 8
title: Sitogilun Malate Plus Amlodipine in Patients With Hypertension and Risk of Early Kidney Damage

brief_summary: This phase 1 study will evaluate a single intravenous infusion of BBM-L101, an investigational AAV-based gene therapy designed to deliver a functional SGCA gene, in ambulatory children aged 4 to \<13 years with genetically confirmed SGCA-related limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD2D/R3). The primary objective is to assess safety and tolerability. The study will also explore muscle protein expression, serum creatine kinase, motor function, biodistribution/vector shedding, and immune responses. Participants will be followed for 52 weeks in the main study and through 5 years after infusion for long-term safety and efficacy.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Dose-Limiting Toxicities (DLTs)
Incidence of Adverse Events (AEs) and Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
title: BBM-L101 Gene Therapy in Participants With LGMD2D/R3

brief_summary:
This pilot study evaluated the feasibility and preliminary outcomes of compassion-focused group therapy (CFT) for adults with depression and/or anxiety who continued to experience symptoms despite previous treatment.

CFT aims to help individuals develop a more compassionate attitude toward themselves and reduce self-criticism and shame, which may contribute to psychological distress.

The study was conducted at a specialized psychiatric outpatient clinic in Stockholm, Sweden, during 2023-2024. A total of 21 participants received an 11-week group treatment consisting of weekly group sessions and brief individual telephone consultations.

The study examined whether participants were willing and able to complete the treatment and whether the treatment was acceptable and feasible in routine psychiatric care. Changes in self-compassion, depressive symptoms, difficulties in emotion regulation, social safeness, everyday functioning, and quality of life were assessed before treatment, immediately after treatment, and three months later.

The findings were intended to inform the further development and evaluation of compassion-focused group therapy for patients with persistent depression and anxiety symptoms.
primary_outcomes: Treatment Completion Rate
title: Feasibility and Preliminary Outcomes of Compassion-Focused Group Therapy for Depression and Anxiety

brief_summary: This study is a single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single ascending dose (SAD) and multiple ascending dose (MAD) clinical trial to evaluate the safety and PK profile in healthy Chinese subjects.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs)
Clinically significant abnormalities
title: A Clinical Study of HH-1270 in Healthy Chinese Subjects

brief_summary:
The aim of this observational study is to monitor the effectiveness of therapy, adherence and safety of a fixed combination of perindopril + amlodipine in patients with essential hypertension. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What is the proportion of patients who achieved reduction of blood pressure to normal values according to ESC guidelines or reduction of systolic pressure by 10 to 15 mmHg and diastolic pressure by 5 to 10 mmHg?
* What is therapy adherence during therapy with fixed combination of perindopril + amlodipine in patients with essential hypertension?
* What is the frequency and types of adverse reactions during therapy with fixed combination of perindopril + amlodipine in patients with essential hypertension? Participants will be followed for twelve months through five measurements (baseline and one, three, six and twelve months after baseline). Values of heart rate and blood pressure, laboratory data (neutrophils, platelets, triglycerides, total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, AST, ALT, urea, creatinine, sodium, potassium, blood glucose), therapy adherence, adverse drug reactions and concomitant therapy will be recorded at each visit.
primary_outcomes: Therapy effectiveness
title: Monitoring the Effectiveness and Safety of Antihypertensive Therapy With a Fixed-Dose Combination of Perindopril and Amlodipine in Patients With Uncontrolled Essential Hypertension

brief_summary: This prospective observational study evaluates three Disease Intervention Specialist service models designed to proactively identify and support adults at risk for substance use disorder. The models include substance use screening, motivational interviewing, case management, treatment referral, and optional peer support. The study will compare participant outcomes across the service models, including substance use severity, treatment engagement, overdose, service utilization, and satisfaction.
primary_outcomes: Severity of Drug Use
title: Disease Intervention Specialist (DIS) for SUD

The name of this program is MAPS (Meaning and Problem Solving). The goal of MAPS is to improve caregivers' emotional well-being and confidence in dealing with adversity. We are testing the program to see if parents and family caregivers find the MAPS program acceptable and identify ways we can improve it.

Intervention and Trial Protocol Acceptability
Satisfaction with Intervention
title: Pilot Trial of a Meaning And Problem-Solving (MAPS) Intervention for Family Caregivers of Children With Medical Complexity

brief_summary: Cataract is the leading cause of reversible blindness and the first surgery worldwide. It corresponds to the crystalline lens opacification. Nevertheless, its grading remains mostly subjective and the Lens Opacities Classification System dating back 1993, is not used in daily practice and has not been revisited since. The HYPERLAF device developed by the start-up HYPEREYE is a modified slit lamp which combines imaging and spectral analysis, providing two quantitative objective scores: OPAK (opacity) and COLOR (spectral analysis). It is a non-CE marked prototype with non-invasive imaging methods.
interventions: Non-contact observation of the crystalline lens nucleus
lead_sponsor: Centre Hospitalier Universitaire de Saint Etienne
primary_outcomes: Reproducibility of COLOR score measurement.
title: Imaging and Spectral Analysis of the Crystalline Lens Using the "HYPERLAF" Slit Lamp

brief_summary: This is a Phase 4, Single Arm Study To Assess The Safety and tolerability of Perioperative Durvalumab in Combination with Neoadjuvant Gemcitabine Plus Cisplatin Treatment Followed by radical cystectomy and Durvalumab alone as Treatment in Indian Patients with Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer. It is to be conducted in compliance with a condition of approval specified by Health Authority of India following the addition of this indication to the approved prescribing information. A phase IV clinical trial to Asses the safety profile of this regimen in patients from India and subsequently, any regulatory action resulting from the review should be complied.
primary_outcomes: Number of subjects experiencing adverse events (AEs)
title: A Prospective, Multi-Center, Phase 4, Single Arm Study To Assess The Safety and Tolerability of Perioperative Durvalumab in Combination With Neoadjuvant Gemcitabine Plus Cisplatin in Indian Patients With Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer Cle-Invasive

brief_summary: Schizophrenia (SZ) is one of the most severe and costly mental disorders in terms of human suffering and societal expenditure. Currently, there are no biomarkers that facilitate the early diagnosis of SZ. Early detection, even before the 6-month duration criteria for diagnosing SZ according to DSM-5, would be crucial for clinician's treatment decisions and patient counselling. While several biomarker candidates have been explored, including those related to neurotransmitter systems, neuroimaging findings, and genetic markers, none have been universally adopted in clinical practice as they lack predictive value. Volatilomics has demonstrated significant potential in refining diagnostic accuracy and improving patient outcomes, especially during the initial stages of SZ. Research has shown differences in Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) like alkanes, ethane, and butane between individuals with SZ and bipolar disorder compared to healthy people. Most important measurement of VOCs is non-invasive, not of any major hurdle to the patient and not time consuming. VOLABIOS will advance the detection and prediction of SZ through the validation and investigation of various VOCs present in different body fluids, opening a diagnostic and prognostic knowledge space within the Patient Journey to measure clinical states and outcome risks with personalised sets of multimodal and validated instruments. Central to its mission is the validation process, conducted across multi-centre trials to ensure the reliability and universal applicability of VOC-based diagnostics.
primary_outcomes: Diagnosis DSM-V
title: Validation and Comparative Multi-Omics Benchmarking of Fluid-Derived Volatilomics Biomarkers for the Prevention and Early Detection of Schizophrenia

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective multicenter observational study is to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of blood-based protein biomarkers for detecting pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in adults aged 18 years and older. The study will investigate whether these biomarkers can help distinguish pancreatic cancer from chronic pancreatitis and mucinous pancreatic lesions, including intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) and mucinous cystic neoplasms (MCNs).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Can blood-based protein biomarkers accurately identify patients with PDAC and distinguish them from patients with chronic pancreatitis or mucinous pancreatic lesions?

Does combining protein biomarkers with CA 19-9 improve diagnostic accuracy compared with using individual biomarkers alone?

Are protein biomarker levels associated with tumor stage, tumor size, or the presence of metastases in patients with PDAC?

Researchers will compare blood levels of protein biomarkers across four groups of patients: those with PDAC, chronic pancreatitis, IPMNs, and MCNs. The biomarkers will include GDF-15, ICAM-1, osteopontin, CXCL10, HGF, Nectin-4, periostin, and VEGF-A.

Participants will:

Provide informed consent before enrollment.

Provide an additional blood sample for protein biomarker measurement, collected alongside routine blood tests and before any oncological or interventional treatment.

Have relevant clinical information, medical history, laboratory results, and imaging findings collected for analysis.
lead_sponsor: Grigore T. Popa University of Medicine and Pharmacy
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Accuracy of Blood-Based Protein Biomarkers for Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
title: Diagnostic Utility of Protein Biomarkers in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Prospective Multicenter Observational Study

brief_summary: This single-arm pre-post study will enroll 50 participants aged 52-65 years who will undergo a 4-week AI-assisted exercise intervention. Postural balance, functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), and three-dimensional motion capture data will be assessed before and after the intervention under different task conditions. During the dual-task condition, the correct response rate (CRR) during serial subtraction of 7 will be recorded. Adverse events occurring during the intervention will also be monitored and recorded.
conditions: Fall Risk in Middle-Aged and Older Adults
primary_outcomes: gait speed
title: Short-term Changes in Postural Sway, Gait, and fNIRS-derived Cortical Metrics After a 4-week AI-assisted Exercise Program: a Single-arm Pre-post Study

brief_summary: This is an open-label, non-inferiority, randomized controlled trial with two parallel arms (experimental and control), following a PROBE (Prospective Randomized Open, Blinded Endpoint) design. The study evaluates whether anticoagulation cessation is non-inferior to anticoagulation maintenance regarding the risk of recurrent thrombosis after antiphospholipid antibodies (aPL) loss in patients with thrombotic antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). Currently, the cornerstone of APS treatment is long-term anticoagulation by vitamin K antagonists (VKAs), which expose patients to the risk of bleeding and have a negative impact on health-related quality of life due to the need for frequent International Normalized Ratio (INR) monitoring. No clinical trial in the existing literature has evaluated anticoagulant cessation after aPL loss. The primary endpoint is the first recurrent thrombotic event during follow-up.
primary_outcomes: First Recurrent Of Thrombotic Event
title: Anticoagulant Cessation After Antiphospholipid Autoantibodies Loss in Thrombotic Antiphospholipid Syndrome

brief_summary:
Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) holds the strongest empirical support for the treatment of Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD). However, in Chile-as in much of Latin America-the availability of DBT falls significantly short of meeting patient demand. Despite its demonstrated efficacy, the duration of DBT and its multicomponent structure pose challenges for implementation and dissemination, particularly within public healthcare settings.

This study aims to compare the clinical effectiveness of a 12-week DBT skills training group (12w-DBT-ST) with a quasi-standard 6-month DBT program (24w-DBT) and treatment as usual (TAU) for individuals with BPD in routine public mental health services. The primary hypothesis is that 12w-DBT-ST will be equivalent to the quasi-standard 24w-DBT and superior to TAU in reducing suicidal and self-harming behaviors.
interventions: Enhanced Dialectical Behavior Therapy Skills Training
primary_outcomes: Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS)
title: Effectiveness of Enhanced Dialectical Behavior Therapy Skills Training Group for Borderline Personality Disorder

brief_summary: Sepsis is a complex syndrome that affects the functioning of multiple organ systems and is caused by an uncontrolled response to infection. Sepsis is usually diagnosed with a physical examination and evaluation of symptoms followed by lab tests to look at how different organ systems are functioning and to look for signs of infection, which can take up to 3 days. There aren't currently any tests that allow doctors to predict patient outcome, hospital course, or severity of illness. Our team has identified a set of genes that when combined can predict the likelihood of clinical deterioration; this set of genes is called SEPSET. In this study the investigators will evaluate the predictive capability of SEPSET along with clinical and laboratory measures in patients with suspected infection.
primary_outcomes: Percent accuracy of the SEPSET 6 gene classifier to predict clinical deterioration when compared to documented clinical deterioration in patients medical charts
title: Clinical Outcomes Using Molecular Prediction in Acute Suspected Sepsis and Infection

brief_summary:
Worldwide, tuberculosis (TB) infection caused by Mycobacterium Tuberculosis, remains one of the top 10 deadly diseases having a significant socioeconomic burden in the world, especially in developing countries. According to global estimates, the latest global TB report indicates that in 2022, roughly 1.3 million individuals died from TB.

The WHO estimated the TB incidence in Egypt in 2019 is 12,000 per 100,000 population. Although Between 1990 and 2019, TB incidence in Egypt declined from 35 to 12 per 100,000 population, while TB mortality declined from 3.5 to 0.43 per 100,000 population. This burden is still a matter of concern, particularly in light of the fact that 66% of TB cases occur among the socially and economically productive age groups of 15-54 years.

TB is a preventable and curable disease, bout 85% of people who develop TB disease can be successfully treated. Anti-tuberculosis chemotherapy is the primary treatment for tuberculosis with first-line drugs, including isoniazid (H), rifampicin (R), pyrazinamide (Z) and ethambutol (E), are commonly used. The WHO recommends (2HRZE/4HR regimen) as a treatment option.

However, Anti-tuberculosis Chemotherapy has serious problems such as disease relapse, the emergence of resistance to drugs and drug-induced liver injury which is a major toxicity of anti-TB treatment.

Among the patients receiving the combination treatment, ATDILI is the most prevalent within the first two months of treatment, which occurs in 4.8% to as high as 36% of patients. Half of ATDILI occurs within 2 weeks of treatment initiation.

Several studies have been conducted in animal models to show the beneficial hepatoprotective effect of some drugs and herbal medicine to prevent and reduce hepatotoxicity from antituberculosis drugs, from these drugs (silymarin and N-acetylcysteine).

It has been proposed that hepatoprotective actions of silymarin may result from the scavenging of free radicals and inhibition of lipid peroxidation, leading to faster recovery after injury.

N-acetylcysteine (NAC) is an antioxidant which exerts its hepato-protective effect by replenishing glutathione stores and enhancing the cellular antioxidant defense mechanism. NAC has been previously studied and used for many years in the treatment of paracetamol-induced hepatotoxicity, with good evidence of efficacy and safety, also was found to be beneficial in non-paracetamol induced acute liver failure. It was demonstrated that the mortality was reduced to 28% using NAC compared to 53% using a placebo.

both silymarin and N-acetylcysteine have been investigated as hepatoprotective agents, but there are relatively few direct head-to-head comparisons in patients receiving anti-TB therapy. Despite the results of animal studies showing the protective effect of silymarin against ATDILI, RCT addressing this issue are limited with inconclusive results. Unfortunately, there are no comprehensive scientific reports on NAC hepato-protective effect on ATDILI.

As there is a lack of randomized controlled trials from Egypt comparing silymarin or N-acetylcysteine for the prevention of Anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury, highlighting the need for locally generated evidence.

Therefore, this study is designed to evaluate the preventive effect of silymarin against the development of ATDH in new TB cases on a standard anti TB drug regimen, also evaluating the effects of NAC on TB treatment.
primary_outcomes: primary outcome will be assessment of the incidence of developing ATDILI.
title: Silymarin Versus N-Acetylcysteine as Protective Effect Against Anti-tuberculosis Drugs Induced Liver Injury.

primary_outcomes: Safety indicators of Phase 1
HBV DNA < LLOQ and HBsAg < LOD, 0.05 IU/mL with or without HBsAb 24 weeks after discontinuation of all CHBs of Phase 2
