brief_summary:
This multicenter prospective observational study will evaluate immune biomarkers in adults undergoing liver transplantation. The study aims to describe how immune markers change before and after transplantation and to assess whether these changes are associated with complications such as infections, acute cellular rejection, and viral reactivation during the first year after transplantation.

Blood samples will be collected before transplantation, on days 0, 3, and 7 after transplantation, and at months 1, 3, 6, and 12. Biomarkers evaluated will include cytokines, interferons, immunoglobulins, lymphocyte populations, monocyte HLA-DR, neutrophil CD64, functional immune assays, checkpoint molecules, and Torque Teno Virus. Clinical outcomes will be recorded prospectively. Biomarker results will be used for research purposes only and will not modify immunosuppressive treatment or other clinical decisions.
primary_outcomes: Longitudinal Change in Early Serum Cytokine and Interferon Concentrations
title: Immune Biomarkers for Predicting Complications After Liver Transplantation

brief_summary: The purpose of this research study is to test how well a new approach - using tools built into the electronic health record (EHR)- can help increase genetic testing for hereditary breast and ovarian cancer (HBOC) in women who have a family history that puts them at higher risk. The study will also look at what helps or gets in the way of using these tools in everyday clinical care. As part of this study, the investigators are also evaluating a website called RealRisks, which is designed to support patients in understanding their risk and making informed decisions about genetic testing. By studying how patients and primary care providers use this tool, the investigators hope to improve the way decision support tools are used to guide conversations and decisions about HBOC testing.
primary_outcomes: Genetic Testing Knowledge
title: EHR Intervention to Increase HBOC Genetic Testing

brief_summary: This study evaluates the feasibility, safety, and predictive role of dynamic bedside Lung Ultrasound (LUS) during therapeutic thoracocentesis in patients with moderate-to-massive pleural effusions. Re-expansion pulmonary edema (RPE) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of rapid pleural fluid drainage. In this single-arm pilot study, participants undergo therapeutic thoracocentesis guided by serial LUS assessments performed at predefined drainage volume milestones (T0: baseline, T1: 500 mL, T2: 1000 mL, T\_3: 1500 mL, and T End). Rather than relying solely on predetermined total drainage limits, procedure modification or early termination is dynamically guided by real-time ultrasound findings (such as coalescent B-lines and subpleural consolidations) alongside clinical monitoring. The main goal is to assess whether serial LUS monitoring can reliably detect early sonographic features of evolving pulmonary edema and inform clinical decision-making during pleural fluid removal.
lead_sponsor: Delta University for Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Total Drained Pleural Fluid Volume
Drainage Velocity
Change in Lung Aeration Score (LUS) Across Procedural Milestones
title: Predictive Role of Lung Ultrasound in Re-Expansion Pulmonary Edema During Thoracocentesis

brief_summary: This study intends to conduct the "Real-world Study on Cervical Cytology Methylation Testing for Endometrial Cancer Screening" project through a multi-center real-world research approach. Led by Peking Union Medical College Hospital, at least 10 institutions will participate in the study. The goal is to complete the enrollment of at least 30 million real-world samples. Focusing on the changes in DNA methylation levels in cervical exfoliated cells as the research entry point, this study aims to provide new ideas and theoretical basis for preventing and treating endometrial cancer by targeting the CDO1/CELF4 double gene methylation. The expectation is to achieve the clinical application of a more optimal endometrial cancer screening protocol, improve the current shortcomings of endometrial cancer screening, make endometrial cancer screening more accurate, effectively reduce the incidence of endometrial cancer, and avoid excessive medical treatment.
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with histopathological diagnosis of endometrial cancer
title: Cervical Cytology DNA Methylation for Endometrial Cancer Screening

brief_summary:
This prospective clinical study will evaluate the effects of moving the entire upper dental arch backward using infrazygomatic crest miniscrews in participants with Class II malocclusion.

Class II malocclusion is a type of bite problem in which the upper and lower teeth do not have a normal front-to-back relationship. Infrazygomatic crest miniscrews provide temporary skeletal anchorage that can be used to move the upper teeth backward while reducing dependence on patient cooperation.

Participants will receive orthodontic treatment using bilateral infrazygomatic crest miniscrews connected to the upper orthodontic archwire through power arms and elastomeric chains. Changes produced by treatment will be evaluated using clinical photographs, radiographs, and digital dental models obtained before distalization and after correction of the Class II molar relationship.

The study will assess dental, skeletal, soft-tissue, and maxillary arch changes associated with this treatment approach.
primary_outcomes: Change in Sagittal Position of the Maxillary First Molar (U6 Crown to Y-Axis)
title: Maxillary Arch Distalization With Infrazygomatic Crest Miniscrews for Class II Malocclusion

brief_summary: The goal of this multicenter randomized clinical trial is to develop and evaluate a web-based stepped-care approach to Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I), specifically tailored to adult cancer survivors experiencing insomnia. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three study arms: stepped-care web-based CBT-I (eSTEPCBT-I), standardized web-based CBT-I (eSTANDCBT-I), or care as usual (CAU). The study aims to determine whether a stepped-care approach can improve access to effective insomnia treatment while maintaining clinical effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.
interventions: Stepped-care Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia
Standard web-based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia
Control arm - Care as usual with sleep hygiene leaflet
primary_outcomes: Insomnia Severity as assessed by the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI)
Insomnia Remission Rate assesed by use of the Insomnia Severity Index (ISI)
title: Effectiveness of a Guided, Web-based, Stepped-care-approach to Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia in Cancer Survivors

brief_summary:
Small amounts of fluid in the knee joint may not always be visible during a standard ultrasound examination performed while the leg is relaxed. When the quadriceps muscle contracts, this fluid may move into the area above the kneecap and become visible. This finding is referred to in this study as occult suprapatellar effusion.

The aim of this study is to determine whether occult suprapatellar effusion is associated with knee pain and physical function in people with knee osteoarthritis. Participants will undergo ultrasound examination first at rest and then during quadriceps contraction. Based on these findings, they will be classified as having effusion visible at rest, occult effusion visible only during muscle contraction, or no effusion in either condition.

Knee pain, self-reported symptoms and function, and chair stand performance will be compared among these groups. The study will also examine whether greater effusion depth is associated with more severe pain, greater functional limitation, and poorer physical performance. No treatment will be assigned as part of the study.
primary_outcomes: Physical Performance Assessed by the 30-Second Chair Stand Test
title: Clinical Importance of Occult Suprapatellar Effusion in Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluates a wearable electrogoniometry-based telerehabilitation system designed to support recovery after total knee arthroplasty. Participants follow the same home-based rehabilitation exercise program and are randomly assigned to an intervention or control group. Participants in the intervention group additionally use a wearable knee device connected to a digital application that provides guidance and real-time feedback during exercise and allows remote monitoring of rehabilitation. Knee range of motion, functional performance, and isometric quadriceps strength are assessed before surgery and during the 12-week postoperative follow-up. The study compares recovery between patients using the technology-assisted rehabilitation system and those following the conventional home-based rehabilitation program.
primary_outcomes: Active Knee Flexion Range of Motion
Passive Knee Flexion Range of Motion
Active Knee Extension Range of Motion
Passive Knee Extension Range of Motion
Isometric Quadriceps Strength
title: Wearable Knee-Assisted Rehabilitation for Range of Motion and Muscle Strength After Total Knee Arthroplasty

brief_summary: The following study aims to standardize the instrumented BBT for the objective evaluation of upper limb joint kinematics using MoCap on a population of healthy subjects between 4 and 18 years of age. After defining normative data characteristic of the gesture, the study aims to characterize the pathological upper limb movement in pediatric subjects with pyramidal hemisyndrome (cerebral palsy, arteriovenous malformation, brain tumors and head trauma) and Down Syndrome, comparing the data obtained with the normative data.
interventions: Inertial Measurement Unit and Box and Block test
primary_outcomes: Smoothness of upper-limb movement measured by the DLJ (dimensionless jerk index)
title: Kinematic Analysis of Manual Dexterity

brief_summary: To evaluate the therapeutic effect of combined oral contraceptive pills in women with benign post-hysterectomy ovarian cysts.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of cyst regression
title: Oral Contraceptive Pills on Woman With Post Hysterectomy Ovarian Cyst

brief_summary: A single-center, single-arm, open-label, fixed-sequence study is planned to enroll 18 healthy participants (6-9 females). The study consists of a screening period, an observation period, and a safety follow-up period.
primary_outcomes: Peak concentration (Cmax)
Area under the serum concentration-time curve from time zero to the last quantifiable concentration (AUC0-t)
Area under the serum concentration-time curve from time zero extrapolated to infinity (AUC0-∞)
title: A Drug-Drug Interaction Study of Rifampicin and Oral HRS-8080

brief_summary:
The primary aim of this study is to evaluate the effects of a controlled breathing exercises-on autonomic nervous system functions (HRV) and perceived stress levels in healthy young adults with dysfunctional breathing patterns.

The secondary objectives of the study are:

* To examine changes in HRV parameters, which serve as an indicator of vagal tone.
* To identify improvements in participants' subjective stress levels and dysfunctional breathing symptoms following the intervention.

This study aims to demonstrate the efficacy of a low-cost, non-invasive, and sustainable respiratory rehabilitation strategy for clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: heart rate variability
heart rate variability
title: The Effect of A Slow-Paced Breathing Intervention on Heart Rate Variability, Stress, and Dysfunctional Breathing Patterns in Healthy Young Adults

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the predictability of preoperative carotid artery-corrected flow time (CFTc) for hypotension after spinal anesthesia in patients undergoing geriatric hip replacement surgery.

Primary outcomes:

• The predictive performance of preoperative CFTc for post-spinal hypotension .

Secondary outcomes:

* Cut-off value, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive value of CFTc in prediction of hypotension.
* Cut-off value, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive value of IVC collapsibility.
* Cut-off value, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value and negative predictive value of echocardiography (ECHO) (LVOT-VTI).
* Comparison of predictive accuracy of CFTc, IVC, and ECHO for post-spinal hypotension.
* Monitoring of systolic blood pressure (SBP), mean arterial pressure (MAP), and heart rate (HR) (first 10 min every 2 minutes, then at 15 min and at 20 min).
primary_outcomes: Predictive Performance of Preoperative Corrected Carotid Flow Time (CFTc) for Post-Spinal Hypotension
title: Carotid Ultrasound for Post-Spinal Anesthesia Hypotension in Elderly Hip Surgery

brief_summary: Successful completion of this project will advance our understanding of the role sympathetic nervous system overactivity plays in driving skeletal muscle malperfusion during hyperinsulinemia and consequently impaired glucose uptake in obesity.
primary_outcomes: Forearm blood flow
title: Peripheral Vascular Effects of Insulin in Obesity

brief_summary: Bruxism and clenching at night and during the day are considered the most common parafunctions that can influence temporomandibular disorders, including chronic myofascial pain of the masticatory muscles. When bruxism and/or clenching are present, treatment generally includes the use of a gnathological splint at night. According to the International Consensus on Bruxism, a definitive diagnosis of bruxism/clenching requires an instrumental assessment consisting of an electromyographic recording of masticatory muscle activity. In this regard, over the past four years, an Italian company (Biotech-Novations, Sanremo, Italy) has created a portable device (dia- BRUXO) to be worn for 24 hours (day and night) that measures muscle activity in the oral region. The company has established baseline cut-off values for daytime and nighttime muscle activity. The aim of the study is to investigate the effectiveness of using gnathological splints in reducing bruxism and clenching during wakefulness and sleep in adults with chronic myofascial pain.
lead_sponsor: Catholic University of the Sacred Heart
primary_outcomes: effectiveness of gnathological splints on bruxism during wakefulness and sleep in adults with myofascial pain, measured through EMG values obtained by dia-BRUXO device. During treatment EMG values will be compared for each subject to pre-treatment EMG
title: Effect Of Orofacial Pain Therapy On Bruxism

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of combining IVR-based rehabilitation with a controlled early active mobilization protocol on functional outcomes, digit range of motion, grip strength, pinch strength and pain following flexor tendon repair.
primary_outcomes: pinch strength(pinch gauge kg)
title: Virtual Reality Combined With Active Mobilization Post Flexor Tendon Repair

brief_summary: A pilot single exploratory clinical trial of ATI in a selected sample of PWH sharing specific genetic, phenotypic and clinical characteristics.
lead_sponsor: Fundacion Clinic per a la Recerca Biomédica
primary_outcomes: Proportion of individuals with VL<50 copies.
title: A Clinical Trial of Analytical Treatment Interruption in People With HIV With a Highly Favourable Profile

brief_summary: This prospective multicentre randomized cross-over post-market clinical follow-up study compares the TASKA GEN2 multi-grip myoelectric hand prosthesis with marketed comparator prostheses in adults with upper-limb amputation. The study evaluates specific function using the Patient-Specific Functional Scale together with upper-limb function, comfort, quality of life, satisfaction and safety outcomes.
interventions: TASKA GEN2 Multi-Grip Myoelectric Hand Prosthesis
Michelangelo or I-Limb Ultra multi-grip myoelectric prosthesis
primary_outcomes: Change in Patient-Specific Functional Scale (PSFS).
title: Cross-Over Study Evaluating the TASKA GEN2 Myoelectric Hand Prosthesis

brief_summary:
MK-2750 is a trial medicine designed to treat certain solid tumors. MK-2750 is a type of treatment called an antibody drug conjugate (ADC). ADCs attach to a protein on cancer cells and deliver medicine to destroy those cells.

The goals of this trial are to learn:

* About the safety of MK-2750 and if participants tolerate it. Tolerate means participants will receive trial treatment in the trial unless they need to stop it due to health problems.
* How many participants have cancer respond (get smaller or go away) to MK-2750
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants Who Experience an Adverse Event (AE)
Number of Participants Who Discontinued Study Intervention Due to an AE
Objective Response Rate (ORR)
title: A Clinical Trial of MK-2750 in Participants With Advanced Solid Tumors (MK-2750-002)

brief_summary: In our study, we investigated upper extremity function and breast cancer-related lymphedema in individuals following breast cancer surgery and treatments
primary_outcomes: upper extremity function- pain and disability
breast cancer-related lymphedema - volume
title: UPPER EXTREMITY FUNCTION AND LYMPHEDEMA IN BREAST CANCER SURVIVORS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY

brief_summary: This study will evaluate the clinical performance and applicability of a large language model-based psychiatric intake support system for caregivers of patients undergoing an initial or re-intake psychiatric evaluation. Caregivers will complete a single adaptive AI interview remotely before the scheduled outpatient visit. The system will generate a structured clinician-facing report and diagnostic screening candidates for nine prespecified target conditions. Treating clinicians will review the AI-generated information while retaining full authority over the final clinical assessment and diagnosis. The system will be evaluated in terms of diagnostic-assistance performance, interview and information-collection performance, documentation quality, acceptability and user experience, and safety.
interventions: LLM-based clinician-in-the-loop psychiatric AI-assisted intake assistance system
primary_outcomes: Pooled sensitivity of AI-generated diagnostic candidates for the nine target disorders
title: LLM Psychiatric Intake AI Clinical Performance Study

brief_summary:
Delirium is a common acute disturbance of attention and cognition among critically ill patients and is associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer hospital stays, and increased mortality. This multicenter, quadruple-masked, randomized controlled trial will evaluate whether 40 Hz gamma auditory stimulation can help prevent delirium in mechanically ventilated adult ICU patients.

A total of 142 participants aged 50 years or older who are expected to require mechanical ventilation for at least 48 hours will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either 40 Hz gamma auditory stimulation or a silent audio track, in addition to standard ICU care. The assigned intervention will be delivered through identical earphones twice daily at 08:00 and 20:00, for 60 minutes per session, until extubation or Day 7 after randomization, whichever occurs first.

The primary outcome is the number of delirium- and coma-free days during the first 7 days after randomization. Secondary outcomes include the incidence and duration of delirium during this period, duration of mechanical ventilation, length of ICU and hospital stay through Day 28, and 28-day all-cause mortality.
primary_outcomes: Delirium- and Coma-Free Days During the First 7 Days After Randomization
title: 40 Hz Gamma Auditory Stimulation for Delirium Prevention in Critically Ill ICU Patients

brief_summary: Epigenetic clocks based on DNA methylation estimate biological age and are associated with age-related conditions, but they have not been validated for female fertility. This prospective, multicenter, observational, non-profit cohort study investigated whether epigenetic age, estimated from peripheral blood DNA methylation, differs between women undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF/ICSI) who achieve a live birth and those who do not. In a predefined subgroup of 30 women under 40 years of age, epigenetic age was also assessed after ovarian stimulation. Participation did not change clinical management.
interventions: Peripheral blood sampling for epigenetic age estimation
lead_sponsor: Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda, Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico
primary_outcomes: Epigenetic age in women with and without live birth after IVF/ICSI
title: Epigenetic Clock to Predict Ovarian Aging and Live Birth in ART

brief_summary:
This Phase 2, multicenter, open-label study will evaluate the safety and efficacy of a single infusion of Prizloncel, an anti-CD19/CD20 chimeric antigen receptor T cells following lymphodepleting chemotherapy in participants with relapsed/refractory (r/r) diffuse large B-cell lymphoma post FDA approved, commercially available CAR T-cell therapy

Approximately 50 participants will undergo leukapheresis, lymphodepletion with fludarabine and cyclophosphamide, and infusion of Prizlon-cel. Participants will be followed for 24 months (approximately 2 years) to evaluate efficacy, safety, CAR T-cell persistence, pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics, and biomarkers. Long-term safety follow-up for gene therapy-related events will continue for up to 15 years following CAR T-cell infusion.
conditions: Relapse Diffuse Large B Cell Lymphoma
HGBL With MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 Rearrangements
primary_outcomes: Overall Response Rate (ORR)
Incidence and severity of adverse events (AEs)
title: Prizloncabtagene Autoleucel (Prizlon-cel) for the Treatment of Relapsed or Refractory Large B-cell Lymphoma Post FDA Approved CAR T-cell Therapy

brief_summary: This monocentric prospective crossover study aims to evaluate the impact of anterior load carriage on gait performance in individuals with unilateral transfemoral amputation using a prosthesis. Participants will complete three randomized walking conditions during a single assessment session: no load, a light anterior load corresponding to 7.5% of body weight simulating child carrying, and a heavier anterior load corresponding to 15% of body weight simulating a utility load. Gait performance, biomechanical adaptations, physiological cost of walking, perceived exertion, and prosthetic comfort will be assessed using instrumented gait analysis and standardized clinical measures. The study seeks to improve understanding of how daily load-carrying tasks affect mobility and balance in prosthetic users and to provide evidence for rehabilitation strategies and prosthetic management.
conditions: Unilateral Transfemoral Amputation in Prosthetic Users
primary_outcomes: Self-selected walking speed (m/s)
title: Impact of Anterior Load Carriage on Gait in Individuals With Transfemoral Amputation

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to understand the effects of developmental powered mobility intervention on global development, gross motor function, and activity performance outcomes in 48 young children (ages 1-2 years) with cerebral palsy (CP). The main question it aims to answer is:

Does the developmental powered mobility intervention produce greater improvements in global development and activity performance outcomes in young children with CP?

How will the developmental powered mobility intervention effect gross motor function?

Researchers will compare the developmental powered mobility (DPM) intervention to usual care physical therapy focused on movement, orientation, repetition, and exercise (MORE-PT) to see if DPM produces greater improvements in outcomes without impeding gross motor function.

Child Participants will:

Receive either DPM or MORE-PT twice weekly for 12 weeks in the home setting.

Complete assessments with the interventionist before and after the 12-week intervention and at a 6-month follow-up visit.

Caregiver participants will: Track outside therapies and any outside assistive device use completed during the intervention, in a weekly log.
primary_outcomes: Bayley Scales of Infant Development-4 (BSID-4)
title: Dynamic, Real-world Learning, Innovative Mobility, and Versatile Exploration (DRIVE): Evaluating a Dose-matched Developmental Powered Mobility Intervention for Young Children With Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary:
Individuals with MS experience significantly high levels of depression which are higher than in any other chronic illness or neurological disorder. Depression can occur at any point in the course of the disease. Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) has been found to be effective in treating depression in people with MS. However, many individuals with MS who would benefit from CBT for depression do not participate in face-to-face treatment due to lack of clinician referral, accessibility, modality preference, cost, and mobility and travel issues due to health reasons.

Given the acceptability and preference for telehealth treatment options, digital-based psychological interventions can be another appealing treatment option as these programs have the ability to deliver interactive CBT treatments for depression to individuals with MS at a time and location convenient to the individual.

The current trial proposes to test the acceptability, effectiveness, satisfaction and cost-effectiveness of an 8-week online depression intervention targeting individuals with multiple sclerosis and compare this intervention with an 8-week online health and wellbeing in MS informational intervention.
interventions: ACTION-MS website - an 8-week cognitive behavioural therapy intervention for depression.
The 'Health and Wellbeing in MS' website
primary_outcomes: Depression, measured on Beck's Depression Inventory II
title: An Online Tailored Cognitive Therapy-Based Intervention for Depression in Multiple Sclerosis: ACTION-MS Online

brief_summary: This study evaluated whether astaxanthin supplementation affects the body's ability to use fat for energy, cognitive performance, and physical function in healthy older adults. In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, participants received both astaxanthin and a placebo during separate study periods. Neither the participants nor the researchers conducting the assessments knew which treatment participants were receiving during each period. Assessments were used to compare outcomes between the astaxanthin and placebo conditions.
primary_outcomes: Respiratory Exchange Ratio During Submaximal Walking
Inhibitory Control Assessed by the Incongruent Flanker Task
Functional Mobility Assessed by the Timed Up and Go Test
title: Effects of Astaxanthin Supplementation on Metabolism, Cognition, and Physical Function in Older Adults

brief_summary:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture is a common and clinically significant injury, particularly among young, active, and athletic adults, and may lead to knee instability and functional impairment. The resulting instability can limit activities of daily living and reduce sports performance, often increasing the need for surgical treatment in physically active individuals. Therefore, ACL reconstruction is widely accepted as an effective treatment option in appropriately selected patients.

In the assessment of patients undergoing ACL reconstruction, not only postoperative clinical success but also the degree of preoperative instability may be important. Determining the effect of preoperative instability severity and side-to-side difference on postoperative functional outcomes, clinical recovery, radiological findings, return to daily activities, and return to sports may provide a more comprehensive and objective evaluation of surgical success.

Although several studies have investigated clinical outcomes after ACL reconstruction, prospective studies evaluating the impact of preoperative instability on postoperative outcomes together with clinical, functional, and radiological parameters remain limited, particularly in our country.

This prospective study aims to investigate the relationship between preoperative knee instability and postoperative clinical, functional, and radiological outcomes in patients undergoing ACL reconstruction at our institution. The findings are expected to contribute to the existing literature and provide useful information for clinical practice.
primary_outcomes: Lysholm Knee Score
International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) Subjective Knee Evaluation Score
title: Evaluation of the Correlation Between Bone Tunnel Projection Placement and Clinical Outcomes in Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Surgery

brief_summary:
Myofascial neck pain may involve several active trigger points in the neck and shoulder muscles. In clinical practice, it is not clear whether treating only the main trigger point that best reproduces the patient's pain is sufficient, or whether treating several active trigger points provides additional benefit.

This randomized controlled trial will compare two trigger point injection strategies in adults with chronic myofascial neck or cervicoscapular pain and active trigger points in at least two different muscles. Participants will receive either a focused injection to the dominant active trigger point or multi-target injections to the active trigger points identified within the study protocol. All injections will be performed under ultrasound guidance using the same local anesthetic and injection technique.

The main outcome will be average pain intensity at 4 weeks. The study will also evaluate early pain response, neck-related disability, global improvement, procedure duration, pain after the procedure, and adverse events.

The study aims to determine whether treating several active trigger points provides enough additional clinical benefit to justify the greater number of injections and increased procedure burden.
primary_outcomes: Average Neck and Cervicoscapular Pain Intensity
title: Focused Versus Multi-Target Trigger Point Injection for Chronic Myofascial Neck Pain

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to investigate the serum levels of lysyl hydroxylase, lysyl oxidase, and the lysyl oxidase-like enzymes in patients with different stages of knee osteoarthritis and to compare these findings with those of healthy control subjects.
primary_outcomes: Biochemical Analysis
title: Lysyl Oxidase and Lysyl Hydroxylase Levels in Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary:
This is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled study. It will test whether remote ischemic conditioning (RIC), a non-invasive arm-cuff treatment, can improve insomnia after ischemic stroke and whether adenosine A2A receptors and neuroinflammation are involved.

About 136 patients will be enrolled. Eligible participants are 18-80 years old, right-handed, have had a first imaging-confirmed ischemic stroke 3-6 months earlier, have an mRS score ≤3, and report insomnia with a PSQI score \>5. Patients with other sleep disorders, severe medical conditions, or recent use of sleep-affecting medications will be excluded.

Participants will be randomly assigned to RIC (cuff pressure 200 mmHg) or sham control (60 mmHg). Both groups will receive treatment twice daily for 90 days. Each session lasts 45 minutes and includes 5 cycles of 5-minute ischemia and 5-minute reperfusion.

The primary outcome is the PSQI score at 90 days. Secondary outcomes include PSQI response (≥5-point decrease), insomnia remission (ISI \<8), polysomnographic sleep measures, fatigue, daytime sleepiness, mood, quality of life, blood inflammatory markers, and A2A receptor expression on monocytes. Follow-up will occur at 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 months.

This study may determine whether RIC is a safe, non-drug option for post-stroke insomnia and help clarify its anti-neuroinflammatory mechanism.
primary_outcomes: Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) Score at 90 Days
title: Adenosine A2a Receptor-Mediated Neuroinflammation in Remote Ischemic Conditioning for Post-Stroke Sleep Disorders

brief_summary: This prospective observational study evaluated whether the preoperative caval-aortic index and pleth variability index can predict post-induction hypotension in adult patients undergoing elective colorectal surgery under general anesthesia. Preoperative caval-aortic index and pleth variability index values were recorded before anesthesia induction. Blood pressure was measured before induction and at 1, 3, 5, 7, and 10 minutes after induction. Post-induction hypotension was defined as a decrease in systolic blood pressure of more than 30% from baseline and/or a mean arterial pressure below 60 mmHg. The predictive performance of the preoperative caval-aortic index and pleth variability index for post-induction hypotension was assessed.
interventions: Preoperative Caval-Aortic Index and Pleth Variability Index Assessment
lead_sponsor: Dr. Lutfi Kirdar Kartal Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Occurrence of Post-Induction Hypotension
title: Preoperative Caval-Aortic Index and Pleth Variability Index for Predicting Post-Induction Hypotension in Colorectal Surgery

brief_summary:
Endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG) is a new mini-invasive technique proposed to treat obesity (1-5). According to the endoscopic procedure compared to videolaparoscopy, this technique is supposed less painful and provide a reduction in postoperative complications (6-7). There are rare informations about the influence of ESG on postoperative painful (8). In this observational pilot study, the investigators prospectively assessed the postoperative analgesia concerns for this recent technique.

The authors evaluated the pain relief, including morphine consumption, pain and satisfaction scores and morbidity following a new endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty scheduled on the first 100 consecutive patients
primary_outcomes: postoperative Morphine consumption
title: Analgesia After Endoscopic Sleeve Gastroplasty

brief_summary: Vitamin D is essential for calcium absorption and bone growth, brain development, and immune system function. Vitamin D is produced by the body in response to natural sunlight. In New Jersey, which is not near the equator and where children are indoors for large parts of the year or use of sun block, it is possible that otherwise healthy children may suffer from vitamin D deficiency, placing them at risk for weak bones, fractures and poor bone growth. Larger children are at a higher risk of deficiency. This research is being conducted to identify children in this group with Vitamin D deficiency and determine the amount of vitamin D supplementation necessary for them daily using a protocol developed.
interventions: Vitamin D3, Calcium, and Vitamin C
primary_outcomes: Measuring serum Vit D and Calcium following supplementation
title: The Effectiveness of a Weight-dependent Algorithm for Dosing Vitamin D.

After an initial brief screen for basic eligibility, participants will be randomized (within site) to either Remote (R) or In-Person (IP) Intake Groups. During the Intake, detailed consent and eligibility assessment will be completed. Participants who are eligible at the Intake will be randomized (within site and Intake Group) to R or IP Treatment and Assessment Groups. Participants will be followed for 3 months.
lead_sponsor: State University of New York at Buffalo
primary_outcomes: Accrual efficiency/Pre-treatment visits
Trial Quality: Retention
Trial Quality: Treatment utilization (patient-reported)
Trial quality: Biospecimen completion rates
title: Remote vs. In-Person Study Evaluation (RISE) Trials: RISE Above Opioid Overdose (Trial 3 of 3)

brief_summary:
Dental caries in primary teeth can sometimes lead to inflammation of the dental pulp, the soft tissue inside the tooth. When the pulp remains capable of healing, pulpotomy may be performed to preserve the tooth until its natural exfoliation. During this procedure, bleeding from the remaining pulp tissue must be controlled before a pulp dressing material is placed.

This randomized controlled clinical trial aims to compare the clinical and radiographic success of TheraCal PT pulpotomy in primary molars when three different solutions are used to control bleeding: 2.5% sodium hypochlorite, 15% ferric sulfate, and normal saline.

Children aged 4-6 years who have primary molars diagnosed with reversible pulpitis and meet the study's eligibility criteria will be enrolled. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups according to the hemostatic solution used during the pulpotomy procedure. TheraCal PT will be used as the pulpotomy material in all three groups.

The treated teeth will be evaluated clinically at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months and radiographically at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. The researchers will compare the outcomes among the three groups to determine whether the choice of hemostatic solution affects the success of TheraCal PT pulpotomy in primary molars.

The findings may help improve understanding of the role of different hemostatic solutions in pulpotomy treatment for primary teeth.
interventions: 2.5% Sodium Hypochlorite applied to pulpal tissue/stumps for 3 minutes to achieve hemostasis prior to TheraCal PT placement during primary molar pulpotomy and 15% Ferric Sulfate (Astringedent™ 15.5%)
primary_outcomes: Overall Clinical Success Rate
title: Effect of Hemostatic Agents on TheraCal PT Pulpotomy Success in Primary Molars

brief_summary:
The goal of this pilot clinical trial is to determine whether radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (rESWT), when used as an adjunct to ultrasound-guided botulinum toxin type A (BoNT-A) injections, can enhance the therapeutic effect of BoNT-A in adults with post-stroke lower-limb spasticity. The study will also evaluate the safety and tolerability of the combined treatment.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the addition of active rESWT to BoNT-A result in a greater improvement in lower-limb spasticity, measured by the change in Modified Ashworth Scale score from baseline to 5 weeks after treatment?
* Does adjunctive rESWT improve other measures of muscle spasticity, ankle mobility, gait performance, perceived global improvement, and pain, and is the treatment safe and well tolerated?

Researchers will compare BoNT-A combined with active rESWT with BoNT-A combined with sham rESWT to determine whether the addition of active rESWT provides greater clinical benefit.

Participants will:

* Receive ultrasound-guided BoNT-A injections according to the study protocol.
* Receive either active rESWT or sham rESWT according to their randomly assigned treatment group.
* Attend scheduled follow-up visits for assessment of spasticity, ankle range of motion, gait performance, muscle length, global clinical improvement, pain, and treatment safety.
* Complete the planned assessments during the follow-up period, including evaluation at 5 weeks after treatment and subsequent follow-up assessments for up to 6 months.
interventions: Radial shock Wave therapy (3000 pulses, 5 Hz, 2.5 bar).
ARM B: Sham-radial shock Wave therapy
primary_outcomes: Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) score
title: Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy as an Adjunct to Botulinum Toxin Type A for Post-Stroke Lower Limb Spasticity (SOLUTION)

brief_summary: This is a single-arm, multicenter, open-label, Phase 1a/1b dose-escalation and dose-expansion study designed to evaluate the safety, preliminary antitumor activity, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) characteristics of NW-301V, an autologous TCR-T cell therapy, in Chinese adult participants with advanced malignant solid tumors harboring a KRAS G12V mutation.
primary_outcomes: Phase 1a: Safety and tolerability of NW-301V in participants with advanced solid tumors
Phase 1a: Maximum tolerated dose (MTD, if applicable) and provisional Recommended Phase 2 Dose (RP2D)
Phase 1b: Safety and tolerability of NW-301V in PDAC, CRC and LUAD respectively under provisional RP2D
Phase 1b: Final RP2D of NW-301V
title: Phase 1 Study of NW-301V TCR-T Cells in Advanced Solid Tumors With KRAS G12V Mutation

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to find out whether a new combination cream containing eflornithine, hydroquinone, and fluocinolone works better and causes fewer side effects than Tri-Luma® (tretinoin, hydroquinone, and fluocinolone), a commonly used treatment for melasma.

The main question is whether replacing tretinoin in Tri-Luma® with eflornithine leads to greater improvement in melasma and less skin irritation over a 12-week period.
primary_outcomes: modified Melasma Area and Severity Index (mMASI) score
Change from baseline in Melanin Index (M) measured using the SkinColorCatch®

brief_summary:
The SPSIP block study aims to systematically describe the distribution of sensory blockade across the region involved in shoulder arthroscopy, as well as the degree of motor sparing of the ipsilateral upper limb and hemidiaphragm. We will assess the sensory response with a cold cotton swab that will be used to compare the sensation of the operated shoulder with that of the opposite (contralateral) shoulder. The patient will be asked whether the feeling of cold is unchanged or altered along the shoulder. This will be tested over an area extending 15 cm anteriorly, laterally and posteriorly. This test will take place 30 min after the SPSIP block. We will also assess the range of motion of the limb undergoing surgery before and after 30 min the anaesthetic procedure. The patient will be asked to perform shoulder abduction and external rotation movements, which the anesthesiologist will explain. We will also measure the diaphragmatic excursion using ultrasound. This procedure will also be performed before and 30 min after the nerve block: the patient will be asked to take deep breaths while the anesthesiologist performs the ultrasound scan.

The study will include adult patients (≥ 18 years) scheduled for shoulder arthroscopy who receive an SPSIP block as the analgesic technique and are able to provide informed consent to study participation and to the processing of personal data will be enrolled.This is a single-centre study conducted exclusively at Piove di Sacco Hospital (Italy).

brief_summary:
This experimental study aimed to determine the effect of virtual museum tours on the psychological well-being and loneliness levels of individuals aged 65 years and older living alone.

Individuals aged 65 years and older who were living alone at home were included in the study. The required sample size was calculated using G\*Power software and determined to be 42 participants, with 21 participants in the intervention group and 21 in the control group. Data were collected using a Personal Information Form, the Psychological Well-Being Scale for Older Adults (YPİOÖ), and the UCLA Loneliness Scale (UCLA-LS). Following the pre-test assessment, participants in the intervention group participated in virtual museum tours through the "Virtual Tour" website provided by the Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Culture and Tourism (https://sanalmuze.gov.tr/?\_Dil=1). The virtual museum tours were conducted once a week for six weeks. After completion of the intervention, the questionnaires were administered again as a post-test. No intervention was applied to the control group until the completion of the study; participants in the control group were subsequently offered the opportunity to experience the virtual museum tour. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, median, frequency, and percentage), Student's t-test, and paired-samples t-test. A p-value of \<0.05 was considered statistically significant. All necessary permissions were obtained prior to conducting the study.
primary_outcomes: Level of psychological well-being
Level of loneliness
title: The Effects of Virtual Tours on Elderly People Living Alone

With sample size determined using G\*Power software to ensure 80% statistical power \& alpha = 0.05), the collected longitudinal data across both groups will be analyzed using Two-Way Repeated Measures ANOVA and student t test between the 2 groups in SPSS to detect significant differences over time and between treatments.

This study aims to evaluate the safety, biodistribution, and imaging characteristics of 18F-N230A PET/CT in patients with suspected or confirmed renal tumors.

Participants enrolled in this study will undergo 18F-N230A PET/CT imaging and 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging. The imaging findings and quantitative parameters will be analyzed and compared. Pathological results obtained from surgery or biopsy will be used as the reference standard to evaluate the potential value of 18F-N230A PET/CT in differentiating renal cell carcinoma from renal pelvic urothelial carcinoma.

This study may provide a new molecular imaging approach for improving the preoperative diagnosis of renal tumors and supporting individualized clinical decision-making.

brief_summary:
Coronary artery disease occurs when the blood vessels supplying the heart become narrowed or blocked. Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a procedure used to restore blood flow to the heart, often by inserting a stent. After PCI, patients are commonly treated with dual antiplatelet therapy, which usually includes aspirin and a second medicine, such as clopidogrel, to reduce the risk of blood clots.

Clopidogrel must be converted by the body into its active form before it can work effectively. An enzyme called CYP2C19 plays an important role in this process. Genetic differences in the CYP2C19 gene can affect how well clopidogrel is activated. Some genetic variations, including CYP2C192 and CYP2C193, are associated with reduced enzyme activity, while CYP2C19\*17 is associated with increased enzyme activity. These differences may influence a patient's response to clopidogrel and could be related to cardiovascular events or bleeding after PCI.

There is limited information about the frequency of these genetic variations and their relationship with clinical outcomes among Egyptian patients receiving clopidogrel after PCI.

The purpose of this study is to determine the prevalence of CYP2C192, CYP2C193, and CYP2C19\*17 genetic variations in Egyptian patients undergoing PCI and receiving clopidogrel. The study will also examine the distribution of CYP2C19 genotypes and predicted metabolizer groups, their relationship with patient characteristics, and their potential association with cardiovascular events, bleeding, and hospitalizations after PCI.

Approximately 1,000 adult Egyptian patients will be recruited from multiple cardiac catheterization centers across Egypt. Information about participants' demographic characteristics, medical history, cardiovascular condition, and medications will be collected. A small blood sample (approximately 3 mL) will be obtained for DNA extraction and genetic testing using a laboratory method called TaqMan real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

Participants' clinical outcomes will be assessed according to the study protocol, including cardiovascular events, heart attack, stent thrombosis, repeat coronary procedures, stroke, bleeding, and cardiovascular-related hospitalizations.

This is a prospective observational study. Participants will receive their clinical care according to the decisions of their treating healthcare professionals. The study will observe the relationship between genetic variations and clinical outcomes; it will not assign treatments based on genetic results.

The findings may improve understanding of CYP2C19 genetic variation in the Egyptian population and provide evidence to support future research on personalized antiplatelet treatment after PCI.
conditions: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI)
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of CYP2C19*2, CYP2C19*3, and CYP2C19*17 Genetic Variants
title: Prevalence of CYP2C19 Genetic Polymorphisms Among Egyptian Patients Receiving Clopidogrel Following PCI
